research.project: N64Recomp (Wiseguy) + N64ModernRuntime + RecompUI / RT64 + the recomp modding framework (and its closest PPC sibling XenonRecomp/UnleashedRecomp)
research.summary: N64Recomp is a static (AOT) recompiler that splits an N64 MIPS binary into individual guest functions using externally-supplied symbol/boundary metadata (today an ELF from a disassembly/decomp; a custom symbol-definition format is planned), then emits one C function per guest function that takes a `(rdram, ctx)` pair where `ctx` is a struct holding every guest register. Translation is deliberately literal and instruction-by-instruction (e.g. `addiu` becomes `ctx->r4 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0x20)`), with `jal`/tail-call `j`/`b` becoming real C calls, `jr` on a recognized jump table becoming a `switch`, indirect calls becoming `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->rX)(rdram, ctx)`, and overlay-relocated immediates becoming `RELOC_HI16/RELOC_LO16` macros resolved at runtime against a live section-load table. A TOML config supplies the non-automatable hints: stubbed functions, skipped functions, single-instruction patches, manual function boundaries, and output mode. The same static-analysis/IR feeds a second backend, the "live recompiler," which uses sljit to JIT x86_64/ARM64 at load time so mods ship as platform-independent MIPS binaries (.nrm) rather than native DLLs. The runtime is N64ModernRuntime (ultramodern = libultra reimpl: threads/audio/RSP tasks/VI; librecomp = overlay handling, PI DMA, saves, relocation macros), graphics go through RT64 (a deferred, full-frame command-list renderer with ubershaders and compute-shader vertex transform), and UI is RecompUI built on RmlUi (HTML/CSS) rendered through RT64. The closest prior art for the PS3 PPU is XenonRecomp/UnleashedRecomp, which solves the exact same big-endian PowerPC + 128-wide vector (VMX128) problem and is the most directly transferable template.

dimensions.dimension: Function detection & boundary recovery (the core of ps3recomp's 72% recall gap)
dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp deliberately does NOT solve function detection itself — it consumes externally-provided boundary+symbol metadata. Today that comes from an ELF produced by a splat-based disassembly or a full decomp project (symbols give name, address, size, section). A planned 'symbol definition file' mode (Issue #13) replaces the ELF with a metadata file carrying: section ROM offsets + base VRAM addresses, each symbol's parent section + VRAM address, sizes for function symbols, and explicit file boundaries (so multiple functions can be emitted per file). XenonRecomp DOES attempt automatic detection via XenonAnalyse: functions with a stack frame have boundaries in the XEX's .pdata exception directory; leaf/frameless functions are found by scanning for branch-link (bl) targets and bounding their length by static flow analysis. Where analysis fails (notably jump-table functions, which look like tail calls), the TOML carries a manual `functions = [{address=.., size=..}]` override list, and an `invalid_instructions = [{data=.., size=..}]` list to skip exception-handler data/padding embedded in the code stream.
techniques: .pdata / exception-directory-driven boundary recovery for framed functions
bl/jal call-target scan + static length analysis for leaf functions
manual function override list in TOML for analyzer failures
invalid_instructions skip-list to step over inline exception/padding data
external symbol-definition file decoupling boundaries from a full decompilation
explicit file-boundary metadata to group functions into translation units
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Directly attacks the documented 72% recall gap. PS3 .opd already gives exported entry points (analogous to .pdata-listed functions); the ~1000 missing functions are exactly the leaf/internal ones reached only by call-target analysis — adopt XenonAnalyse's two-tier strategy: (1) parse .opd + any EH frame info as authoritative boundaries, (2) do a fixpoint bl/branch-target scan to discover internal callees, (3) expose a TOML `functions=[{address,size}]` manual list plus an `invalid_instructions` skip-list so Ghidra-found-but-tool-missed functions can be hinted by hand instead of blocking the build. Critically, adopt N64Recomp's philosophy: do not try to make the tool a perfect disassembler — make boundary metadata an explicit, hand-editable input.

dimensions.dimension: Config / TOML hint system (manual overrides, patches, stubs)
dimensions.howItWorks: Both tools centralize all human-supplied knowledge in a single TOML. N64Recomp's TOML: input/output paths, stub-out-function list, skip-recompilation list, single-instruction patch list, and a single-file output mode toggle. XenonRecomp's TOML is richer: [main] (file_path, patch_file_path, patched_file_path auto-generated, out_directory_path, switch_table_file_path), [optimizations] booleans (skip_lr, skip_msr, ctr_as_local, xer_as_local, cr_as_local, reserved_as_local, non_argument_as_local, non_volatile_as_local), register save/restore entry addresses (restgprlr_14_address, savegprlr_14_address, restfpr/savefpr, restvmx/savevmx, restvmx_64/savevmx_64 — each identified by a documented byte pattern like `e9 c1 ff 68`), longjmp_address/setjmp_address for native redirection, the manual functions list, invalid_instructions list, and a separate switch_table TOML referenced by path. Mid-asm hooks are TOML stanzas (see hooks dimension).
techniques: single authoritative TOML driving the whole build
function stub list (replace body with no-op/HLE)
function skip list (provide hand-written replacement instead)
single-instruction patch list (fix one bad opcode without touching source)
byte-pattern signatures to auto-locate compiler runtime helpers (savegpr/restgpr etc.)
optimization flags that trade output size/speed (local-register promotion removed ~20MB)
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp should grow an equivalent TOML layer over elf_parser/find_functions output. High-value additions mapped from XenonRecomp: (1) byte-pattern detection of GCC/SNC PPU runtime helpers (_savegpr/_restgpr/_savefpr/_restfpr, _savevr/_restvr for VMX) so calls to them can be inlined or stubbed — these are huge sources of phantom 'functions' and ABI noise on PPC; (2) stub/skip lists so any LV2 syscall or HLE NID that can't be lifted gets a hand-written C body; (3) single-instruction patch list to neutralize unliftable opcodes; (4) optimization toggles (e.g. treat CR/XER/CTR/LR as locals when a function provably has no exception path) — on PPC this is the single biggest perf win because it deletes the save/restore helper traffic.

dimensions.howItWorks: Each guest function becomes one C/C++ function with a fixed signature: N64Recomp uses `void fn(uint8_t* rdram, recomp_context* ctx)`; XenonRecomp uses `(PPCContext& ctx, uint8_t* base)`. The context struct holds the entire guest register file — GPRs, FPRs, vector registers (VR/VMX), CR fields, XER, LR, CTR (and MSR/reserved on PPC). Emission is literal and per-instruction: rabbitizer (N64) / a PPC decoder (Xenon) decodes, then a fixed C template per opcode is printed using helper macros (ADD32, S32, etc.) so wrap/sign/zero-extension semantics are explicit. Branch delay slots are handled by duplicating the delay-slot instruction at each branch path. Output is intentionally not human-readable. XenonRecomp adds a key perf lever: register classes (CR/XER/CTR/LR/non-volatiles) can be promoted from struct fields to C local variables per-function when safe, letting the host compiler keep them in registers and eliminating save/restore-helper calls.
techniques: one C function per guest function, uniform (mem, ctx) signature
context struct = full guest register file, passed by pointer/reference
literal per-opcode template emission via semantic macros (ADD32/S32/...)
delay-slot duplication (MIPS) / explicit flag computation (PPC CR)
per-function promotion of register fields to C locals for host register allocation
host compiler (Clang/MSVC/GCC) does the real optimization, not the recompiler
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is exactly ps3recomp's model (ppu_context*/spu_context*). Two concrete upgrades from XenonRecomp: (1) The PPU has 32 GPRs + 32 FPRs + 32 VMX vectors + CR/XER/CTR/LR — keeping all of CR/XER/CTR/LR as memory fields and recomputing condition codes on every compare is brutally slow on a register-starved x86-64 host (16 GPRs). Implement the same per-function 'as_local' promotion analysis: when a function has no path that escapes/observes a flag register, hold it in a C local. XenonRecomp reports this is the dominant optimization. (2) Make condition-code emission lazy: only materialize CR bits that a later branch actually reads, exactly the kind of dataflow XenonRecomp's local-promotion enables.

dimensions.dimension: VMX / VMX128 vector SIMD lifting (maps to PPU AltiVec/VMX)
dimensions.howItWorks: XenonRecomp implements each VMX/VMX128 instruction with host x86 SSE/AVX intrinsics directly, and gets ARM64 'for free' via SIMD Everywhere (simde), which provides x86-intrinsic shims on NEON. The hard part is endianness: rather than byte-swapping each 32-bit lane, the recompiler reverses the ENTIRE 16-byte vector once on load/store, which means every vector instruction implementation must account for reversed lane order (e.g. dot products use the W/Z/Y components instead of X/Y/Z; pack instructions take reversed arguments). It also manages an FPU subtlety: scalar FP must preserve denormals while VMX flushes them, so the current FP/denormal-flush mode is stored in the context and toggled around instructions as needed. Some exotic D3D pack/unpack vector ops only support a subset of operand types; unimplemented cases emit a compile-time warning or a debug-break in the output.
techniques: 1:1 VMX-instruction-to-x86-intrinsic mapping
SIMD Everywhere (simde) to retarget x86 intrinsics onto ARM64 NEON
whole-16-byte vector reversal instead of per-lane swap for big-endian
lane-order compensation baked into each vector op (WZY vs XYZ)
denormal-flush mode stored in context and toggled per scalar/vector op
warning/debug-break emission for unimplemented opcode/operand variants
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: The PPU's VMX/AltiVec is essentially the same ISA family as VMX128 (minus the 128-register extension), so XenonRecomp's vector lifter is near-drop-in prior art for ps3recomp's VMX handling. Steal three things verbatim: (1) the whole-vector-reversal endianness trick — it dramatically simplifies the lifter versus per-lane swaps and matches the PPU's big-endian vector layout; (2) the simde dependency to cover ARM64 hosts without writing NEON paths; (3) the per-instruction denormal-flush toggling, since PPU AltiVec also flushes denormals while scalar FP does not. The SPU's custom 128-bit SIMD ISA is a different opcode set but the SAME engineering pattern applies: 1:1 map SPU vector ops to SSE/AVX/NEON intrinsics, reverse-whole-vector for endianness, and emit warning/debug-break stubs for unimplemented ops.

dimensions.dimension: Indirect branches, jump tables, and virtual/function-pointer calls
dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp turns a `jr` into a C `switch` when it can prove the register came from a jump table, and turns genuine indirect calls (`jalr $25`) into `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r25)(rdram, ctx)`, where LOOKUP_FUNC is a runtime address-to-function-pointer resolver. XenonRecomp detects jump tables by pattern-matching `mtctr r0` (almost always followed by `bctr`) with preceding address-computation, then XenonAnalyse emits a separate switch-table TOML (referenced by switch_table_file_path) that lets the recompiler generate a real C switch. For arbitrary indirect/virtual calls, XenonRecomp builds a 'perfect hash table' at runtime: dereferencing a 64-bit pointer at (original_instruction_address * 2) yields the recompiled function's address; the function-address region is placed just past the valid XEX memory region in the base pointer and exported as macros in ppc_config.h (a previous design that reserved 8GB of virtual address space was abandoned for memory-pressure reasons).
techniques: static jr/bctr-with-jump-table -> C switch conversion
mtctr r0 / bctr pattern detection for table discovery
externalized switch-table TOML (tool-generated, human-fixable)
guest-address -> recompiled-function-pointer lookup (LOOKUP_FUNC)
perfect hash via address*2 indexing into a table past the guest memory region
function-pointer table base exported as a generated header macro
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the documented hard case for ps3recomp (function pointers / vtables / switch tables). Adopt the same split: (1) emit C switches for statically-resolvable PPC jump tables — on PPC look for the analogous `mtctr`/`bctrl` pattern plus the lwz/add address computation; (2) for everything else, build a guest-EA -> host-function-pointer table indexed off the address space. The address*2 perfect-hash-past-memory-region trick is directly applicable because the PS3 guest address space is 32-bit-addressable within the mapped region (host_ptr = g_base + guest_addr), so reserving a function-pointer table just past the mapped region and indexing by guest EA is feasible. Also adopt the externalized, tool-generated-but-hand-editable switch-table file so unresolved tables can be patched in config rather than blocking the build.

dimensions.dimension: Overlays, relocations & dynamically-loaded code (maps to SPU local-store loading)
dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp supports both statically-linked and relocatable overlays. For relocatable overlays, instructions carrying a relocation (lui, addiu, loads/stores) are emitted with macros instead of constants: `lui $24,0x80C0` becomes `ctx->r24 = S32(RELOC_HI16(1754, 0x630) << 16)`, paired with RELOC_LO16, so the runtime fixes up the immediate based on where the section is currently loaded. The runtime maintains a live table of which sections are loaded and at what address; LOOKUP_FUNC resolves overlay function pointers against that table. librecomp in N64ModernRuntime owns overlay handling and PI DMA (the mechanism by which overlays are paged in from ROM). The symbol-reference-file mechanism (PR #82) lets the recompiler resolve symbols/relocations against one binary while recompiling another — the basis for compiling patches/mods without the original ELF and auto-applying relocations.
techniques: relocation-aware emission: RELOC_HI16/RELOC_LO16 macros instead of baked constants
runtime section-load table for address fixup
LOOKUP_FUNC resolving overlay functions against the load table
PI-DMA modeling for paging overlay code/data from ROM
cross-binary symbol/relocation resolution (recompile A, resolve against B)
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: The SPU problem (code DMA'd into 256KB local store at runtime, hard to find statically) is structurally the N64 relocatable-overlay problem at a larger scale. Borrow: (1) emit relocation-bearing instructions as macros, not constants, so SPU code lifted from one location can be relocated; (2) maintain a runtime local-store-load table mapping (SPU id, LS offset) -> currently-resident module so a guest-EA->function resolver can dispatch DMA'd-in code that was recompiled ahead of time from a known module catalog; (3) the cross-binary symbol-reference mechanism (PR #82) maps almost exactly onto PS3 HLE: recompile a game module while resolving its imports/relocations against a separate symbol set (the LV2/firmware module exports), eliminating the need to have every dependency's binary present. For SPU modules that genuinely cannot be found statically, the same TOML manual-function + skip approach applies: catalog known SPU programs (e.g. from EDGE/SPURS jobs) and recompile each as a separately-loadable unit.

dimensions.dimension: Big-endian handling at the memory boundary
dimensions.howItWorks: XenonRecomp keeps all instruction implementations operating on little-endian (host-native) values, and does the byte swap only at the memory boundary: every load swaps big->little on read, every store swaps little->big on write. All such loads/stores are marked `volatile` specifically to stop Clang from reordering them in unsafe ways. Vectors are handled by whole-16-byte reversal rather than per-element swaps (see VMX dimension). This isolates endianness to exactly two choke points (load helper, store helper) plus the vector load/store path.
techniques: swap-at-boundary only (registers/ops stay host-endian)
volatile-qualified guest memory accessors to block unsafe reordering
whole-vector reversal for 128-bit values
centralized load/store helper functions as the single swap site
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already does 'big-endian conversion at memory boundaries' — XenonRecomp validates that exact choice and adds two refinements worth copying: (1) mark the guest load/store accessors volatile so the host compiler can't hoist/reorder them across MMIO-like or self-modifying-code-sensitive points (relevant for RSX register pokes and SPU channel/DMA); (2) use whole-16-byte reversal for VMX/SPU 128-bit values instead of 4x32 lane swaps, which is both faster and simpler, at the cost of compensating lane order inside each vector op.

dimensions.dimension: Mid-asm hooks & function patching/override (HLE + game fixes)
dimensions.howItWorks: XenonRecomp's mid-asm hooks let you inject a native C++ call at an arbitrary instruction address via a TOML stanza: [[midasm_hook]] with name, address, registers (the guest regs passed as PPCRegister& args), and a mutually-exclusive control directive — return, return_on_true/return_on_false, jump_address, jump_address_on_true/on_false, and after_instruction (place call after vs before the instruction). The recompiler inserts the call; the user implements the function. For whole-function override it aliases the function to an __imp__ implementation and weakly links the original, so a custom C++ definition wins at link time while still being able to call the original (PPC_FUNC/PPC_FUNC_IMPL macros). N64Recomp's modding layer formalizes this into preprocessor attributes: RECOMP_HOOK / RECOMP_HOOK_RETURN (before/after a target function), RECOMP_PATCH (replace a same-named ROM function), RECOMP_EXPORT / RECOMP_IMPORT (mod-to-mod and mod-to-base symbol sharing, '*' = base recomp, '.' = self), and an event system (RECOMP_DECLARE_EVENT / RECOMP_CALLBACK).
techniques: TOML-declared mid-asm hooks at arbitrary instruction addresses
register-list argument passing into native hook functions
control-flow directives (return/jump, conditional, before/after)
weak-link + __imp__ aliasing for full-function override with super-call
macro attributes for hooks/patches/exports/imports and an event/callback bus
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the mechanism ps3recomp needs for HLE and incremental bring-up. Map: (1) mid-asm hooks = a clean way to intercept a syscall trampoline or a known busy-wait/sync primitive and replace it with host behavior without lifting it; (2) weak-link/__imp__ override = the right pattern for resolving NIDs — emit a weak default body for each imported NID and let a hand-written HLE library override it, with the original recompiled body still callable when the lib wants to fall through; (3) the single-file output mode (below) plus link precedence means HLE/patch C can be authored once and always beats the auto-generated body. Adopt the TOML mid-asm-hook schema verbatim for surgical fixes (e.g. patch out an LV2 spin-wait, redirect cellGcmSys flip to the host backend).

dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp offers a mode that emits all functions into one file (vs the default one-file-per-function), used for building compiled patches. It exploits standard linker behavior: a linker only pulls a symbol from a static library if it wasn't already defined by an earlier input. By feeding the recompiled patch objects to the linker BEFORE the bulk recompiler output (packaged as a static lib), any patched function transparently overrides the original. This makes patch iteration fast because you only recompile the changed functions, not the whole binary.
techniques: single-file emission mode for patch sets
link-order precedence (objects before .a) to override without editing generated code
incremental recompile of only changed functions
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Directly improves ps3recomp's iteration loop. Package the bulk per-function output as a static library and link any hand-written/HLE/override C ahead of it; then fixing a mislifted function or supplying an HLE body never requires regenerating or editing the giant generated tree. This pairs with the weak-link override pattern and is essentially free to implement (it's a build-system convention, not a code feature).

dimensions.dimension: Dual backend: static C + 'live recompiler' (sljit JIT) sharing one IR
dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp added a 'live recompiler' that JITs x86_64/ARM64 at runtime via sljit, but it is explicitly still STATIC recompilation: it reuses the same static analysis and instruction-translation logic as the C backend (a shared IR feeds both the C emitter and the sljit emitter). It's slower than the AOT C path but fast enough for large code volumes. Its purpose is mods: modders ship a platform-independent MIPS binary (.nrm) and the runtime live-recompiles it on load, so no per-platform DLLs are needed and recompilation bugs can be fixed in the runtime without re-shipping mods. Validation uses a per-instruction test corpus (input regs/memory + expected outputs) from an N64 CPU test repo.
techniques: shared static-analysis/IR feeding both AOT-C and JIT backends
sljit as a portable JIT codegen target (x86_64 + ARM64)
load-time recompilation of platform-independent guest binaries for mods
instruction-level differential test corpus for backend validation
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Two transferable ideas. (1) Architect ps3recomp's lifter around a shared IR so the same PPU/SPU translation can drive an AOT C emitter today and a JIT later — this also makes it natural to add a fallback interpreter/JIT for code that can't be found statically (the SPU dynamic-loading and indirect-branch gaps), which is otherwise fatal to a pure-AOT design. (2) Build an instruction-differential test harness from real hardware/RPCS3 traces (input context+memory -> expected output context) per PPU/SPU opcode; the scene treats this as the correctness backbone and ps3recomp will need it given VMX/SPU edge cases (the N64 div sign-extension test failure shows how granular this catches bugs).

dimensions.howItWorks: The runtime is split: ultramodern reimplements libultra core (threads, controllers, audio, message queues, timers, RSP task handling, VI timing) with platform I/O delegated to the host project via callbacks and graphics delegated to an external renderer (RT64). librecomp bridges recompiled code to ultramodern and adds overlay handling, PI DMA (ROM reads), EEPROM/SRAM/Flashram saving, and the rest of libultra. Recompiled functions receive `rdram` (the guest RAM base) and `ctx`; guest pointers are offsets into rdram. The runtime owns the section-load table that RELOC_*/LOOKUP_FUNC resolve against, and the mod loader plugs the live recompiler in here.
techniques: two-layer runtime: HW/OS reimpl (ultramodern) + recomp bridge (librecomp)
rdram base pointer passed to every function; guest pointers = offsets
host I/O via callbacks; renderer is pluggable
runtime-owned section-load table for relocation/lookup resolution
OS-thread / message-queue / timer reimplementation matching the guest OS API
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Mirrors ps3recomp's vm-memory model (host_ptr = g_base + guest_addr) and validates passing the memory base to every function. The two-layer split is the right organizing principle: a 'cellmodern' layer reimplementing LV2/firmware primitives (threads, sync, mailboxes, lwmutex, SPU thread groups, timers) with host-callback I/O, and a 'librecomp'-style bridge owning syscall dispatch, module/PRX load tables (the relocation/lookup base), and save/VFS. The N64 OS-thread reimplementation is a concrete template for emulating PS3 sys_ppu_thread/sys_spu_thread via host threads while keeping the guest OS API surface intact.

dimensions.dimension: Graphics: RT64 deferred command-list renderer (maps to RSX NV47 FIFO)
dimensions.howItWorks: RT64 never issues draws immediately; it logs the entire frame's command history into an auxiliary structure first, then optimizes/enhances/replaces before submitting to the GPU. It splits into a deferred RDP (memory reads + texture ops queued, flushed only on RDP full-sync, enabling GPU-side memory copies and pattern detection) and a deferred RSP that runs all vertex transforms (position/lighting/texturing) in a GPU compute shader. It uses ubershaders to avoid pipeline-compilation stutter, targets D3D12/Vulkan/Metal behind an RHI ('plume') abstraction, does texture replacement via bindless texture arrays, and generates interpolated frames by matching draw calls across frames (textures, transform, velocity) for high-framerate rendering.
techniques: defer entire frame's command stream, then analyze/optimize before GPU submit
RDP deferral flushed on full-sync to batch and detect memory patterns
RSP vertex transform moved to a GPU compute shader
ubershaders to eliminate pipeline-compilation hitches
RHI abstraction (plume) over D3D12/Vulkan/Metal
bindless texture arrays for replacement; cross-frame draw matching for interpolation
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: The RSX is an NVIDIA NV47 FIFO command processor — ps3recomp already plans to parse the FIFO and replay on a backend. RT64's deferred, whole-frame command-list model is the proven architecture for exactly that: parse the entire GCM/FIFO command buffer into an internal command list, then translate/optimize/replay on D3D12/Vulkan rather than translating each FIFO method eagerly. Borrow: (1) defer and batch — flush on RSX sync/flip events (analogous to RDP full-sync); (2) put an RHI between the command translator and the backends so null/D3D12/Vulkan share one frontend (matches ps3recomp's planned multi-backend); (3) ubershaders to avoid PSO-compile stutter when translating RSX shader programs; (4) a frame debugger that dumps the captured command list is invaluable for bring-up. The compute-shader-vertex-transform idea is less relevant (RSX has real programmable shaders), but the defer-then-replay command-list spine is directly applicable to FIFO parsing.

dimensions.dimension: Mod packaging & UI framework (RecompUI on RmlUi via RT64)
dimensions.howItWorks: Mods are .nrm files = renamed zips containing a JSON manifest (target game id, mod id, version, author), an optional mod symbol file + self-contained MIPS mod binary, optional texture/patch files, and a thumbnail. RecompModTool builds them from a mod.toml. The live recompiler turns the shipped MIPS into native code at load. Mods can be normal (live-recompiled), offline-recompiled to a DLL, or ship custom binaries. UI is RecompUI, an API over RmlUi (a lightweight C++ HTML/CSS UI library that builds a DOM, handles events, and outputs vertices/indices/draw-commands); RecompUI renders by building RT64/plume command lists and exposes recompui.h so mods can build in-game UI. Other mod APIs: recomputils.h (alloc/util), recompconfig.h (config options, incl. enum options like a texture-pack toggle), recompdata.h (data structures). Texture packs are .rtz files.
techniques: zip-based mod container (.nrm) with JSON manifest + optional code/assets
platform-independent mod code via live-recompiled MIPS (no native DLL needed)
RmlUi (HTML/CSS DOM) for UI, rendered through the game's own RHI
stable mod C API surface (utils/config/data/ui) shared across all recomps
config-option system with typed options (enum toggles, etc.)
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Lower priority for ps3recomp's current tier (no game boots yet), but the architecture is worth pre-planning: an HTML/CSS UI lib (RmlUi) rendered through the same RHI you use for RSX gives config/overlay menus cheaply and consistently. The more immediately useful idea is the stable mod/HLE C API surface and the .nrm-style 'ship guest code, recompile on load' model — for PS3 this maps to distributing per-title patch/HLE bundles that the runtime resolves against firmware symbol sets (PR #82 mechanism). Defer this until boot works.

dimensions.howItWorks: The scene strictly separates concerns into composable tools: a ROM/binary splitter + disassembler (splat) to get boundaries/symbols; the recompiler (N64Recomp/XenonRecomp) for CPU code; a separate RSP/microcode recompiler (RSPRecomp) for the signal processor; XenonAnalyse as a standalone analysis pass that emits a switch-table TOML consumed by the recompiler; RecompModTool for packaging; the runtime and renderer as independent libraries integrated via CMake add_subdirectory. XenonRecomp pins Clang 18+ and relies on compiler-specific intrinsics; N64Recomp is more compiler-portable (MSVC/GCC/Clang) and depends on rabbitizer (decoder), ELFIO, toml11, fmtlib.
techniques: decoupled tools (splitter / analyzer / recompiler / packager / runtime / renderer)
separate co-processor recompiler (RSPRecomp) distinct from main-CPU recompiler
analysis pass emits machine-readable hints (switch-table TOML) consumed downstream
off-the-shelf deps: rabbitizer decoder, ELFIO, toml11, fmtlib, sljit, simde, RmlUi
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already mirrors this (elf_parser / find_functions / ppu_lifter / spu_lifter as separate stages). Reinforce two patterns: (1) keep the SPU recompiler a fully separate tool from the PPU one (as RSPRecomp is separate from N64Recomp) since SPU's ISA/memory/DMA model is alien to the PPU's; (2) make analysis passes emit hand-editable hint files (function lists, switch tables, jump-table descriptions) rather than burying decisions in code — this is what lets the community incrementally fix the 28% of functions auto-detection misses. Consider adopting rabbitizer-equivalent maturity for the decoder and simde to avoid hand-writing NEON.

standoutInnovations: Make function boundaries an EXPLICIT, hand-editable input, not something the tool must perfectly infer: N64Recomp refuses to be a disassembler and instead consumes symbol/boundary metadata, with TOML manual-function and invalid-instruction lists as escape hatches. This directly defuses ps3recomp's 72%-recall blocker — partial auto-detection + human hints beats waiting for perfect detection.

XenonRecomp's per-function promotion of CR/XER/CTR/LR/non-volatile registers from context-struct fields to C local variables, which lets the host compiler register-allocate them and DELETES all save/restore-helper calls (reported ~20MB output shrink). This is the single biggest PPC perf lever and applies verbatim to the PS3 PPU.

Byte-pattern signatures to auto-locate and special-case compiler runtime helpers (__savegprlr/__restgprlr/__savefpr/__savevmx etc.) — turning ABI boilerplate into intrinsic save/restore instead of phantom functions. PS3 GCC/SNC emit the analogous _savegpr/_restgpr/_savevr helpers.
Whole-16-byte vector reversal for big-endian (instead of per-lane swap), with lane-order compensated inside each vector op — simpler and faster, directly reusable for PPU VMX and SPU 128-bit SIMD.

Perfect-hash indirect-call table: index by (guest_instruction_address * 2) into a function-pointer region placed just past the guest memory mapping; abandoned an 8GB virtual reservation for this. Maps cleanly to PS3's g_base + guest_addr layout for resolving vtables/function pointers.

Relocation-as-macro emission (RELOC_HI16/RELOC_LO16 + runtime section-load table + LOOKUP_FUNC) for relocatable overlays — the structural template for PS3 SPU code DMA'd into local store and PRX relocation.

Cross-binary symbol-reference recompilation (PR #82): recompile module A while resolving symbols/relocations against module B's symbol set — exactly the NID/HLE import-resolution and patch-without-original-binary workflow ps3recomp needs.

Single static IR feeding BOTH an AOT-C backend and an sljit-based JIT 'live recompiler', enabling platform-independent shipped guest code and an obvious path to a JIT/interpreter fallback for statically-unfindable code (the SPU dynamic-load gap).
Patchable single-file output exploiting linker symbol-precedence (patch objects before the bulk static lib) so overrides/HLE/fixes never require editing or regenerating the generated tree.

RT64's defer-the-whole-frame-then-replay command-list architecture — the proven model for ingesting a GPU FIFO (RSX NV47) command stream, optimizing it, and replaying on D3D12/Vulkan/Metal behind one RHI.
verifiableClaims: N64Recomp emits one C function per guest function with signature taking (uint8_t* rdram, recomp_context* ctx), translating instructions literally (e.g. addiu $r4,$r4,0x20 -> ctx->r4 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0x20)), and converting jalr indirect calls to LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r25)(rdram, ctx) and relocated lui to RELOC_HI16(...) macros.

XenonRecomp's documented top optimization is promoting CR/XER/CTR/LR and non-volatile registers to C local variables (cr_as_local, xer_as_local, etc.), which removes register save/restore helper calls and reduces executable size by roughly 20MB; it requires Clang 18+ and uses SIMD Everywhere (simde) to run x86 VMX intrinsics on ARM64.

XenonRecomp resolves indirect/virtual calls via a runtime 'perfect hash table' indexed by (original instruction address * 2), with the function-pointer region placed past the valid XEX memory in the base pointer and exported as macros in ppc_config.h, after abandoning an earlier 8GB virtual-allocation approach.

N64Recomp's 'live recompiler' uses the sljit library to JIT x86_64/ARM64 at load time but is still static recompilation (reuses the same static analysis as the C backend), and exists so mods ship platform-independent MIPS binaries (.nrm) rather than per-platform native libraries.

RT64 defers all draw calls into a full-frame command-history structure before GPU submission, runs RSP vertex transforms in a GPU compute shader, uses ubershaders to avoid pipeline-compilation stutter, and targets D3D12/Vulkan/Metal; RecompUI is built on the RmlUi HTML/CSS library and renders through RT64.

research.project: Zelda 64 Recompiled (Majora's Mask / Ocarina of Time) + N64Recomp + RT64 renderer
research.summary: Zelda 64: Recompiled is a finished, shipping product built on three decoupled pieces: N64Recomp (a static/AOT MIPS-to-C recompiler), N64ModernRuntime (the host runtime providing memory, syscalls/HLE, save/input), and RT64 (a modern D3D12/Vulkan/Metal renderer that translates N64 RDP/RSP graphics to GPUs). The recompiler does a deliberately *literal* per-instruction translation (one C function per guest function, taking `(rdram, recomp_context* ctx)`), emitting macros like `ADD32`, `MEM_W`, and `LOOKUP_FUNC` rather than a fancy IR, which keeps the lifter simple and lets the host C compiler (MSVC/GCC/Clang) do the optimization. Crucially it does NOT solve function detection itself — it leans on an external symbol oracle (an ELF from the Majora's Mask decompilation/splat), and handles indirect control flow with a mix of static jump-table->switch detection and a runtime `LOOKUP_FUNC` address->function-pointer table that also makes relocatable overlays and live mods work. RT64 is the most transferable single idea for RSX: it is a *deferred* renderer that logs an entire frame's draw calls into an auxiliary history structure, runs dual renderers (native-res for RAM correctness + high-res for enhancement), moves vertex transform (RSP) and texture decode (TMEM) onto GPU compute, and matches draw calls across frames for interpolation and ray tracing. The modding layer (RECOMP_PATCH/HOOK/EXPORT/IMPORT, .nrm packages, extended GBI) is a fully-realized UX that ps3recomp can copy wholesale.

dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp deliberately does NOT do robust automatic function discovery. It requires a list of symbols + metadata (currently from an ELF) that names every function and its address range, then 'splits the input binary into functions that are each individually recompiled into a C function, named according to the metadata.' For Zelda64Recomp these symbols come from the Majora's Mask decompilation project (a pinned decomp commit) and live in syms.toml (function defs the recompiler uses to find code in the ROM) plus datasyms.toml / datasyms_static.toml (used during patch recompilation to resolve data/function references). So the hard recall problem is offloaded to a separate, mature decomp/splat toolchain rather than being solved inside the recompiler.
techniques: external symbol oracle (ELF from decompilation) instead of in-recompiler heuristics
TOML symbol files: syms.toml for code-finding, datasyms*.toml for reference resolution
pin to a specific decomp commit hash for reproducibility
separate the 'where are the functions' problem from the 'translate the function' problem
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Directly attacks ps3recomp's #1 gap (function-detection recall ~72%, missing ~1000 fns Ghidra finds). Lesson: don't try to make find_functions.py perfect; treat function discovery as a pluggable symbol-oracle stage and accept symbols from an external tool. For PS3 that oracle is Ghidra (which already finds the missing ~1000) and the .opd table — export a Ghidra symbol map (or IDA) into a TOML/JSON the lifter consumes, and let call-target analysis from Ghidra fill in the non-.opd, non-standard-prologue functions. The recompiler then only needs to be correct given a function list, not discover it.

dimensions.howItWorks: Translation is intentionally literal and one-instruction-at-a-time: each MIPS instruction emits a line of C using macros. Example: `addiu $r4,$r4,0x20` -> `ctx->r4 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0x20);`. The register file is a plain struct `recomp_context` with `gpr r0..r31` (gpr = uint64_t), `fpr f0..f31`, `hi`, `lo`, `status_reg`, and a `mips3_float_mode` flag. Arithmetic correctness is encoded in macros (`ADD32(a,b) = (gpr)(int32_t)((a)+(b))` to get MIPS 32-bit sign-extension-into-64-bit semantics; `S32/U32/S64/U64/SIGNED` for width/sign casts). `jal` -> direct C function call; `j`/`b` recognized as tail calls -> function call; delay slots handled by duplicating the delay-slot instruction at each branch path. The literal style means the host C compiler does all real optimization.
techniques: one C function per guest function, signature `f(uint8_t* rdram, recomp_context* ctx)`
macro-encoded semantics (ADD32/SUB32/S32/U32) instead of IR — keeps lifter tiny
delay-slot handling by instruction duplication on each branch edge
tail-call recognition turns j/b into C calls so the host stack mirrors the guest
let the C compiler optimize; lifter stays 'dumb but correct'
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's ppu_lifter.py already emits one C fn per guest fn with ppu_context* — same shape. Adopt the macro-semantics discipline: encode PPU quirks (32-bit ops on 64-bit GPRs, XER carry/overflow, CR field updates, rlwinm masks) as macros so the lifter stays literal and the compiler optimizes. Delay slots don't exist on PPU, but the tail-call-as-C-call trick is directly applicable and helps the host optimizer. The closest prior art is still XenonRecomp/UnleashedRecomp (Xenon = PowerPC + VMX128) which mirrors this exact literal-macro approach for a PPC core — study its VMX128 macro set for the VMX/AltiVec lifter.

dimensions.dimension: SIMD (VMX/AltiVec on PPU; SPU vector ISA)
dimensions.howItWorks: N64 has no real SIMD on the CPU (the VR4300 FPU is scalar 32/64-bit), so N64Recomp's CPU path gives little SIMD guidance. The relevant SIMD handling is in two places: (1) the RSP, a 128-bit vector co-processor with its own microcode, recompiled by a SEPARATE tool path (RSPRecomp / rsp_recomp.cpp) into C; and (2) RT64 moves the vertex/lighting math (the bulk of RSP vector work) to GPU compute shaders instead of emulating the vector unit on CPU at all. The fpr union (double d / {float fl, fh} / {u32 l,h} / u64) shows the pattern for type-punning a register that's read as different widths.
techniques: separate recompiler binary for the vector co-processor (RSP) vs the main CPU
fpr as a union for read-as-float/read-as-double/read-as-int type punning without UB-prone casts
offload vector workloads to GPU compute rather than scalar-emulating the vector ISA
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Maps to two distinct PS3 problems. For PPU VMX/AltiVec (128-bit): lift to host SIMD intrinsics or `std::simd`, and use union-style vector registers like the fpr union to handle the many sub-element views (vector of 4 floats / 8 shorts / 16 bytes). The XenonRecomp VMX128 lifter is the canonical reference. For SPU: N64Recomp's lesson is structural — treat the SPU like RT64 treats the RSP: a *separate* recompiler path with its own context, not bolted onto the PPU lifter. ps3recomp already has spu_lifter.py; keep it independent, give it its own 256KB local-store address space and channel/mailbox runtime, mirroring how RSPRecomp is a distinct tool from the CPU recompiler.

dimensions.dimension: Indirect branches (function pointers, vtables, switch/jump tables)
dimensions.howItWorks: Two-pronged. STATIC: the recompiler 'attempts to turn a jr instruction into a switch-case statement if it can tell it's being used with a jump table' (pattern-matches the lui/addiu/sll/lw sequence that loads from a jump table). DYNAMIC: anything it can't prove statically becomes a runtime lookup. `jalr $25` -> `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r25)(rdram, ctx);` where `LOOKUP_FUNC(val) = get_function((int32_t)(val))`. The runtime 'maintains a list of which program sections are loaded and at what address' and resolves the guest address to the correct host C function pointer. This same table is what makes relocatable overlays and live-loaded mods callable.
techniques: jump-table pattern recognition -> native switch/case
runtime address->function-pointer table (get_function) for all unresolved indirect calls
the lookup table doubles as the overlay/mod relocation mechanism
register the guest entry address of every recompiled function so any guest pointer can be called
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the cleanest answer to ps3recomp's 'indirect branches hard to resolve statically' gap. Build a global guest-address -> host-function-pointer registry populated at startup for every lifted function; compile every `bctr`/`bctrl`/`blr`-through-pointer and every vtable/switch-table call into a `LOOKUP_FUNC`-style runtime resolve. You do NOT need to statically prove every indirect target — you only need every *reachable function* registered (which ties back to using Ghidra's call-target analysis to enlarge the function list). PS3 .opd entries (function descriptor = {entry, TOC}) make this even cleaner: the descriptor address is a natural key. Keep the static jump-table->switch optimization for hot dispatch but fall back to the registry for everything else.

dimensions.howItWorks: Guest RAM is a flat host buffer (`rdram`) passed to every function. Address translation is baked into macros: `MEM_W(offset,reg) = *(int32_t*)(rdram + (((reg)+(offset)) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000))`. The constant subtraction maps the N64 KSEG0 virtual base (0x80000000, sign-extended) to host offset 0. Endianness is handled per-access for sub-word loads via XOR on the low address bits: `MEM_H` uses `^2`, `MEM_B` uses `^3` (the classic big-endian-in-a-little-endian-buffer trick) — so the backing store is kept in one byte order and only narrow accesses are fixed up, avoiding a full byteswap of every store. The recomp_context is a per-thread register file; HLE/syscalls are C functions the recompiled code calls directly.
techniques: flat guest RAM buffer + constant-offset base subtraction folded into MEM_* macros
XOR-on-address (^2/^3) endianness fixup for sub-word access instead of byteswapping every value
per-instruction inline memory macros (no software MMU/TLB walk on the hot path)
register file as plain struct passed by pointer (recomp_context*)
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already uses host_ptr = g_base + guest_addr — same flat-buffer idea. The transferable refinement is the XOR-address endianness trick: PS3 is big-endian and the host is little-endian, so instead of byteswapping at every memory boundary (the doc's stated approach), store guest memory in native guest byte order and XOR the low address bits for narrow accesses, OR (better for PPU's 64-bit world) keep data little-endian and byteswap only at load/store macros. Either way, fold the base+endian fixup into MEM_B/H/W/D macros so the lifter stays literal. The 'register file = struct passed by pointer' and 'HLE = direct C call' patterns match ps3recomp's design exactly.

dimensions.howItWorks: N64 has no OS, but N64Recomp reproduces the same dynamic-symbol pattern: special guest addresses act as import stubs. Recompiled-runtime functions are assigned synthetic addresses in the 0x8F000000 range (e.g. `recomp_puts = 0x8F000000;`), so when guest code calls them, the LOOKUP_FUNC/get_function path routes to a native C implementation. The runtime intercepts the N64's RSP/RDP *audio* microcode by replacing it with C implementations that interface with modern audio libraries, and graphics by routing display lists to RT64. Mods extend this with RECOMP_IMPORT/RECOMP_EXPORT where '*' means a base-recomp export and '.' means the mod's own native library.
techniques: synthetic guest address ranges (0x8F000000+) as import/intercept points
HLE by symbol-name -> native C function, resolved through the same function-lookup table
intercept audio/graphics microcode at the subsystem boundary and replace with native libs
namespaced import resolution ('*' base, '.' self, 'modname' for cross-mod)
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Maps cleanly onto ps3recomp's NID/HLE layer. PS3 already resolves HLE libs via 32-bit NID = SHA1(name)[:4]; treat each resolved NID exactly like N64Recomp's synthetic-address imports: register the NID (or a synthetic address) in the same function-lookup table the indirect-call path uses, so cellXxx calls and guest indirect calls share ONE dispatch mechanism. Adopt the 'intercept at subsystem boundary' rule: don't try to recompile cellGcmSys/cellAudio/cellVdec PPU code — stub the NID to a native HLE that talks to the RSX command processor / FFmpeg / host audio, exactly as RT64 replaces RSP/RDP audio with C+modern libs.

dimensions.dimension: Graphics (RDP->GPU; analog to RSX NV47 FIFO->backend)
dimensions.howItWorks: RT64 is a DEFERRED renderer: instead of immediate-mode submitting RDP commands, it logs an entire frame's draw calls into an auxiliary history structure, enabling optimization, asset replacement, interpolation and ray tracing. Key mechanisms: (1) Deferred RDP — memory/texture reads are queued and only flushed on full RDP sync, letting it detect GPU-side copies and replace patterns. (2) Deferred RSP (compute) — ALL vertex transform/lighting/texturing runs in a GPU compute shader, freeing the CPU and enabling high poly counts and frame-gen. (3) Dual renderers — one at native res that syncs back to RAM immediately (so games reading framebuffers get correct data), one at high res/high framerate for display. (4) Texture decode — raw 4KB TMEM uploaded to GPU and decoded to RGBA32 by compute shader (one of the most accurate TMEM loaders, RE'd from console + Wiseguy test ROMs). (5) Framebuffer detection — tracks memory ranges as framebuffers, does GPU copies + per-pixel reinterpretation compute shaders for format reinterpretation/post-processing. (6) RDP color-combiner (newcolor=(A-B)*C+D) and blender modes become generated GPU shaders/pipelines keyed by mode. (7) Extended GBI — extra commands hidden behind a NOOP (safe on real HW) like gEXVertexZTest for widescreen/interpolation. (8) Path tracing — merges compatible draw calls into scenes, builds BLAS via compute (transform to world space), assembles a TLAS for real-time path-traced lighting.
techniques: frame-wide draw-call history buffer (defer everything, optimize the recorded frame)
GPU compute for vertex transform AND texture decode (move the vector co-proc work to GPU)
dual renderer: native-res copy keeps guest RAM correct, hi-res copy is for display
framebuffer tracking + reinterpretation compute shaders
shader/pipeline generation keyed on combiner+blender mode, cached
extended command set tunneled through a hardware-safe NOOP
draw-call matching across frames (params/texture/position/velocity) for interpolation + motion vectors
BLAS-from-untransformed-vertices via compute, TLAS per scene for path tracing
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: RT64 is the single richest source of transferable architecture for the RSX backend. ps3recomp parses the NV47 FIFO into commands — make that backend DEFERRED like RT64: record a frame's command stream into a history structure before translating, so you can batch, dedupe, do framebuffer-effect detection, and add enhancements. Steal: (a) compute-shader vertex transform (RSX vertex programs) and compute texture decode for RSX's swizzled/tiled formats; (b) dual-renderer pattern to keep guest RAM framebuffers correct for games that read them back (PS3 does this constantly for post-fx); (c) generate-and-cache D3D12/Vulkan PSOs keyed on RSX combiner/blend/fog state, the direct analog of RT64 keying pipelines on the RDP combiner+blender mode; (d) framebuffer range tracking for render-to-texture. The deferred-frame model also future-proofs the planned Vulkan backend. RT64 even has a Vulkan/D3D12/Metal abstraction layer worth studying as the backend interface shape.

dimensions.howItWorks: The N64's audio is generated by RSP audio microcode + RDP. The recomp handles audio by 'replacing the N64's RSP and RDP audio processing with C implementations that interface with modern libraries,' i.e. it does NOT recompile/emulate the audio microcode instruction-by-instruction; it HLEs the whole audio subsystem at the API boundary and renders through a host audio library, while preserving accurate output. (There is also an aspMain TOML config, indicating the audio microcode path is recognized and intercepted as a named overlay.)
techniques: HLE the audio microcode/subsystem rather than LLE-recompiling it
named-overlay config (aspMain.*.toml) to recognize and intercept the audio task
render through a modern host audio library for sample-rate/latency flexibility
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: PS3 audio is cellAudio + (for some titles) SPU-side mixing/decoding. Lesson: HLE cellAudio at the NID boundary to a host audio library rather than relying on recompiled SPU mixer code, the same way RT64/recomp HLE the RSP audio task. For SPU audio DSP that's genuinely custom, the named-overlay-intercept pattern (aspMain.toml) maps to detecting a known SPU audio module by signature and swapping a native implementation. This sidesteps part of ps3recomp's incomplete cellAdec/cellVdec problem for the audio half.

dimensions.howItWorks: Fully-realized, this is the project's flagship UX. Patches are source-level macros compiled against the symbol files: RECOMP_PATCH (replace an original function), RECOMP_FORCE_PATCH (override even a base-patched fn, discouraged), RECOMP_HOOK("FuncName") and RECOMP_HOOK_RETURN("FuncName") (run code before/after a target without replacing it), RECOMP_EXPORT (expose a fn to other mods), RECOMP_IMPORT("modname", sig) (call into base recomp via '*', own native lib via '.', or another mod by name), RECOMP_DECLARE_EVENT + RECOMP_CALLBACK (a pub/sub event system between mods). Mods ship as .nrm packages built by RecompModTool from a TOML; a mod is itself a small *relocatable* recompiled MIPS binary (its symbol file describes sections + relocations so multiple mods load into the address space simultaneously via the same RELOC_HI16/RELOC_LO16 + function-lookup machinery). Mods may bundle platform-native DLL/.so/.dylib for offline-recompiled or native code, picked by the runtime per platform. Two mods patching the same function are flagged incompatible. Install by drag-and-drop onto the window.
techniques: source macros (RECOMP_PATCH/HOOK/HOOK_RETURN/EXPORT/IMPORT/DECLARE_EVENT/CALLBACK) resolved against symbol files
mods are relocatable recompiled binaries -> reuse the overlay relocation + function-lookup system
.nrm package + JSON manifest (game id, mod id, version, deps, exports, imports)
RecompModTool builds packages from TOML; can also recompile RSP microcode
optional native shared libs per platform alongside the .nrm
automatic incompatibility detection when two mods replace the same function
drag-and-drop install UX
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Even though ps3recomp hasn't booted a game, this is the end-state UX to design toward and it costs little to scaffold now because it REUSES the same primitives ps3recomp needs anyway. The function-lookup registry built for indirect branches becomes the patch/hook injection point: RECOMP_PATCH = register a host fn at a guest .opd address overriding the default; RECOMP_HOOK = wrap the registry entry. Treat a mod as a relocatable PPC blob loaded via the same loader used for the main image. The NID import mechanism already gives you RECOMP_IMPORT('*', ...). Adopt the JSON manifest + drag-and-drop + 'two mods touching one fn = incompatible' policy verbatim — it's proven and low-risk.

dimensions.howItWorks: Everything is driven by TOML. The recompiler takes a TOML specifying input/output paths, functions to stub out, functions to skip recompiling, and single-instruction patches (patch an instruction in the target binary). Symbols are split across syms.toml (find code) and datasyms*.toml (resolve data/refs). RSP microcode and audio tasks get their own per-task TOMLs (aspMain.us.rev1.toml, njpgdspMain.us.rev1.toml, us.rev1.toml). Output mode: every recompiled function is emitted into its own .c file (with planned grouping for build speed); a single-file output mode lets you compile patched functions separately and have the linker prioritize them over the original output — that's the link-time override mechanism for patches. Build is CMake. RecompModTool (separate binary, also TOML-driven) packages mods.
techniques: TOML as the single config surface for recompiler behavior (stub/skip/patch lists, IO paths)
per-overlay/per-microcode TOMLs keyed by region+revision (us.rev1)
one-.c-file-per-function output for incremental builds
single-file output + linker symbol priority as the patch-override mechanism
instruction-level patch list in config (fix a bad instruction without touching the lifter)
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's Python pipeline (elf_parser.py/find_functions.py/ppu_lifter.py) should grow an equivalent declarative config: a TOML/JSON listing stubbed NIDs, skipped functions, per-instruction patches, and per-overlay (PRX/SPU-module) symbol sets keyed by title+region. The 'single-file output + linker priority' trick is a clean, build-system-only way to override a mis-lifted function with a hand-written C one — very useful while recall/correctness are improving. Per-task TOMLs map to PS3's many PRX modules and SPU programs; key them by title id + version like us.rev1.

dimensions.dimension: Overlays / relocatable code (analog to PS3 PRX + SPU dynamic loading)
dimensions.howItWorks: N64 games stream code overlays into RAM at runtime, so the recompiler can't bake absolute addresses. For relocatable sections it emits relocation macros instead of constants: `lui $24,0x80C0` in a section based at 0x80BFA100 becomes `ctx->r24 = S32(RELOC_HI16(1754, 0x630) << 16);` (and the paired low half via RELOC_LO16), where 1754 is the section index. At load time the runtime fixes these up to the actual load address and registers the section in the loaded-sections list that LOOKUP_FUNC consults. RSP microcode is recompiled too, though RSP *overlay* support is explicitly not yet implemented.
techniques: RELOC_HI16(section_index, offset) / RELOC_LO16 macros emitted in place of absolute address immediates
runtime tracks loaded sections + their actual addresses; LOOKUP_FUNC resolves calls into them
section-index-keyed relocation lets the same code run at any load address
mods reuse this exact mechanism to load alongside the base game
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the template for two PS3 problems. (1) PRX modules (PS3's dynamically-linked relocatable libraries): emit RELOC-style macros for address-bearing immediates in PRX code and fix them up when the PRX is 'loaded' into the guest address map, registering its functions in the lookup table. (2) SPU dynamically-loaded code (ps3recomp's noted gap: SPU code is DMA'd into local store at runtime and is hard to find statically): you cannot statically know where an SPU module lands in the 256KB local store, so adopt the same relocatable-section model for SPU — recompile each known SPU module as a relocatable unit and relocate/register it when the PPU DMAs it in, rather than trying to resolve a fixed local-store layout statically. The 'RSP overlays not yet supported' caveat is a warning that this is the hardest part and may need a dynamic/interpreter fallback for unknown SPU blobs.

dimensions.howItWorks: Save data is stored separately from the game in a platform-standard config dir (Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Zelda64Recompiled\saves, Linux ~/.config/..., macOS ~/Library/Application Support/...), so updating the binary preserves saves; an autosave system respects the original owl-save semantics (replaces the previous autosave/owl save). Input adds modern affordances on top of the N64 controller model: dual-analog camera (right stick), gyro aiming for first-person items (DS4/DualSense/Switch Pro), keyboard/mouse, all exposed to mods through recomp API calls (recomp_get_gyro_deltas, recomp_get_target_framerate, recomp_get_window_resolution). Framerate is decoupled from the original tick rate via RT64 (play at any framerate), and load/pause/transition are near-instant since there's no disk/cart emulation overhead.
techniques: saves stored outside the binary in OS-standard per-user dirs -> updates don't wipe saves
autosave layer that honors the original game's save semantics
modern input layered over the guest controller API and exposed via recomp_* calls to mods
framerate decoupled from guest tick rate by the renderer
recomp_* host API surface (input/timing/window) callable from recompiled code and mods
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Even pre-boot, ps3recomp should define this contract early: emulate PS3 save-data (cellSaveData) into OS-standard per-user dirs so the model is right from day one; expose a recomp_*-style host API (input via cellPad/cellKb/cellMouse HLE, timing, window) that both recompiled code and future mods call. Framerate decoupling depends on the renderer being deferred (see Graphics) — another reason to build the RSX backend RT64-style. The broader lesson: the 'finished product' polish (saves survive updates, modern input, instant loads) comes almost free once the HLE + lookup-table + deferred-renderer foundations are right, so design those three to also serve UX, not just correctness.

dimensions.dimension: Closest prior art for the PPU lifter (Xenon/PowerPC)
dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp is MIPS, not PowerPC, so its specific opcode handling doesn't transfer, but its ARCHITECTURE (literal per-instruction macros, struct register file, function-lookup table, separate vector co-proc recompiler, external symbol oracle) is shared with the PowerPC-targeting recomps. The same author/community decompose problems identically across MIPS (N64Recomp), the renderer (RT64), and the PowerPC family. The PowerPC-specific work to study is XenonRecomp/UnleashedRecomp (Sonic Unleashed PC port), which statically recompiles Xbox 360 Xenon PowerPC + VMX128 to C using this same family of techniques.
techniques: reuse the N64Recomp structure (literal macros + lookup table + external symbols) but swap the ISA frontend
study XenonRecomp for PPC GPR/CR/XER/FPSCR macro encodings and VMX128 SIMD lifting
treat VMX128 like RSP/SPU: a vector unit with its own well-defined macro set
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's PPU is 64-bit PowerPC + VMX/AltiVec — essentially the same CPU family as Xenon (PowerPC + VMX128). XenonRecomp/UnleashedRecomp is therefore the single closest real-world reference for ppu_lifter.py: it already solves big-endian PowerPC -> little-endian-host C, CR/XER condition handling, and VMX128 -> host SIMD, all in the literal-macro style N64Recomp pioneered. Concretely: borrow XenonRecomp's PPC instruction-to-macro tables and its VMX register/intrinsic mapping, and borrow N64Recomp's runtime patterns (lookup table, MEM_* endianness macros, RELOC macros for PRX). Combining the two covers most of ps3recomp's PPU + indirect-branch + relocation needs.

standoutInnovations: Literal per-instruction translation with semantics in macros (ADD32, S32, MEM_W) instead of a heavyweight IR — the lifter stays tiny/auditable and the host C compiler (MSVC/GCC/Clang) does all optimization. Directly applicable to ps3recomp's PPU/SPU lifters.

A single runtime function-lookup table (get_function/LOOKUP_FUNC: guest address -> host fn pointer) is the ONE mechanism that simultaneously solves indirect branches, function pointers/vtables, relocatable overlays, AND live mod injection. ps3recomp should build this once and reuse it for bctr/bctrl, NID HLE, PRX loading, and mods.

Offloading function DISCOVERY to an external symbol oracle (decomp ELF / splat; for PS3, Ghidra+.opd) instead of trying to make in-tool boundary detection perfect — directly addresses ps3recomp's 72% recall gap.

RT64's deferred-frame renderer: log an entire frame's draw calls into a history structure, then optimize/enhance/interpolate/ray-trace it. The dual-renderer split (native-res for RAM correctness + hi-res for display) is the key trick for games that read back their own framebuffers — exactly what PS3 post-fx does.

Moving the vector co-processor's work (RSP vertex transform) AND texture/TMEM decode to GPU compute shaders rather than CPU-emulating them — maps to handling RSX vertex programs and swizzled-texture decode on the host GPU.

RELOC_HI16(section_index, offset)/RELOC_LO16 macros emitted in place of absolute-address immediates, fixed up at load time — a clean static-recomp answer to relocatable code that maps to PS3 PRX modules and (critically) to SPU code DMA'd into local store at unknown addresses.
XOR-on-address endianness fixup in MEM_H(^2)/MEM_B(^3) macros: keep the backing store in one byte order and only patch sub-word access addresses, avoiding a full byteswap on every store.

A complete, low-risk modding UX (RECOMP_PATCH/HOOK/HOOK_RETURN/EXPORT/IMPORT/DECLARE_EVENT/CALLBACK + .nrm packages + JSON manifest + drag-and-drop + automatic same-function-conflict detection) built entirely on top of the relocation + lookup-table primitives the recompiler already needs.

Extended GBI commands tunneled through a hardware-safe NOOP so enhanced display lists still run on real N64 — a pattern for adding host-only render features (widescreen, frame-gen hints) without breaking guest semantics.

Treating the vector/audio co-processor as a SEPARATE recompiler path (RSPRecomp distinct from the CPU recompiler; audio HLE'd at the subsystem boundary) — validates keeping ps3recomp's spu_lifter.py independent and HLE-ing cellAudio rather than LLE-recompiling SPU mixers.
verifiableClaims: N64Recomp's recomp_context stores GPRs as uint64_t (gpr) and FPRs as a union {double d; struct{float fl,fh;}; struct{uint32_t u32l,u32h;}; uint64_t u64;}, with a mips3_float_mode flag and an f_odd pointer, confirming union-based float/double type punning and explicit MIPS3 float-mode handling.

Memory access macros bake the KSEG0 base offset into the access and use XOR address fixup for endianness: MEM_H uses (addr ^ 2) and MEM_B uses (addr ^ 3), subtracting 0xFFFFFFFF80000000 to index the rdram host buffer.

Indirect calls compile to LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r25)(rdram, ctx) where LOOKUP_FUNC(val) = get_function((int32_t)(val)), and the runtime resolves the guest address against a list of loaded sections/addresses — the same table used for overlays and mods.

Relocatable overlay code emits RELOC_HI16(section_index, offset) and RELOC_LO16 macros in place of absolute-address immediates (e.g. lui $24,0x80C0 -> ctx->r24 = S32(RELOC_HI16(1754,0x630) << 16)), fixed up at load time by the runtime.

RT64 performs vertex transformation (position/lighting/texturing) on a GPU compute shader (deferred RSP) and uploads raw 4KB TMEM to the GPU for compute-shader texture decode to RGBA32, and it runs two simultaneous renderers (native-res synced to RAM + high-res/high-framerate for display).

research.project: XenonRecomp + XenonAnalyse (Xbox 360 / Xenon PowerPC -> C++), with supporting analysis of UnleashedRecomp (runtime/HLE), XenosRecomp (GPU shader recomp), and N64Recomp (prior art)
research.summary: XenonRecomp is a static (AOT) recompiler that converts Xbox 360 XEX executables into per-guest-function C++ files, where every recompiled function has the uniform signature `void func(PPCContext& ctx, uint8_t* base)`. The Xenon CPU is a 3-core PowerPC with VMX128 SIMD, which makes it the closest possible prior art for a PS3 PPU (PowerPC + VMX/AltiVec) lifter. The pipeline is: XenonAnalyse statically discovers functions (via the XEX `.pdata` exception table plus branch-link scanning and control-flow walking) and detects jump tables (by pattern-matching `mtctr`/`bctr` sequences) emitting a TOML file; XenonRecomp consumes a hand-augmentable TOML config (explicit function sizes, switch tables, save/restore-helper addresses, longjmp/setjmp addresses, invalid-instruction skips, mid-asm hooks, register-localization optimization flags) and emits C++ via a giant per-opcode switch that writes string templates. Memory is a flat `base + guest_addr` mapping with byteswap baked into every load/store macro; vectors are stored fully byte-reversed; VMX is lifted to SSE/NEON via SIMDE; FPU-vs-VMX denormal-flush mode is tracked with a compile-time CSR state machine to elide redundant rounding-mode writes. Indirect calls resolve through a runtime "perfect hash" function-pointer table keyed by guest address, and the companion UnleashedRecomp supplies the HLE/kernel layer with `GUEST_FUNCTION_HOOK` macros and `HostToGuestFunction`/`GuestToHostFunction` templates that marshal PPC registers to/from native C++ ABI. Nearly all of this maps directly to ps3recomp's PPU lifter, and the trampoline/import model maps to the NID/HLE layer; SPU and RSX need adaptation (SPU has no PowerPC analog; RSX maps to XenosRecomp's shader-recomp idea rather than CPU recomp).

dimensions.howItWorks: Two-tier discovery. Tier 1: functions that use stack space are listed in the XEX `.pdata` segment (the Windows-style exception/unwind table), giving exact start+size for free. Tier 2 (functions absent from .pdata): XenonAnalyse scans the code section for branch-link (`bl`) instructions, treating each call target as a candidate function start, then runs `Function::Analyze(code, size, base)` which walks instructions from the start address. Analyze maintains a worklist (`blockStack`) of basic blocks: it follows fall-through and branch targets, treats `bl`/`bctrl` (isLink set) as non-terminating calls, and terminates a block on unconditional `b`, `blr` (`PPC_OP_CTR` with xop 16/528), or a zero word (padding). Conditional branches (`bc`) push BOTH the fall-through block (`(addr-base)+4`) and the taken target (`addr + PPC_BD(insn) - base`). A `projectedSize` mechanism extends the function end when a branch target lies beyond the current end. Finally blocks are sorted by address and discontiguous trailing blocks are discarded, yielding a contiguous [base, size). The recompiler additionally identifies the compiler's shared register save/restore helper runs (restgprlr_14/savegprlr_14/restfpr/savefpr/restvmx/savevmx) by fixed byte-pattern signatures (e.g. restgprlr_14 begins `e9 c1 ff 68`) given as addresses in the TOML, so calls into them are understood rather than mis-parsed.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Directly transferable to ps3recomp's find_functions.py, which currently sits at ~72% recall vs Ghidra. PS3 ELFs carry the .opd (official procedure descriptor) table = the natural analog of .pdata for seeding starts; the project already uses it but should ALSO (a) harvest every `bl` target as a candidate start (catches the ~1000 call-reachable functions with no .opd entry and no standard prologue — exactly the gap named in broad-testing-findings.md), and (b) run a Xenon-style block-walk to derive size instead of relying on prologue matching. The save/restore-helper signature trick maps to PPC64 ELF's __savegpr_*/__restgpr_* / _savefpr/_restfpr millicode and the VMX save/restore stubs — detecting and special-casing them prevents boundary errors. The 'manual size override in TOML' escape hatch is a cheap, high-value way to reach the last few hard functions without improving the heuristic.

dimensions.dimension: Jump tables / switch tables (indirect intra-function branches)
dimensions.howItWorks: XenonAnalyse (XenonAnalyse/main.cpp) detects computed-goto switch tables by sliding-window pattern matching on decoded opcodes. It defines opcode-sequence masks for four variants: SWITCH_ABSOLUTE = [LIS, ADDI, RLWINM, LWZX, MTCTR, BCTR]; SWITCH_COMPUTED = [LIS, ADDI, LBZX, RLWINM, LIS, ADDI, ADD, MTCTR]; SWITCH_BYTEOFFSET = [LIS, ADDI, LBZX, LIS, ADDI, ADD, MTCTR]; SWITCH_SHORTOFFSET/word = [LIS, ADDI, RLWINM, LHZX, LIS, ADDI, ADD, MTCTR]. A `SearchMask()` pass finds a match; `ScanTable()` then scans BACKWARD up to ~32 instructions to find the bound check `cmplwi crX, rY, N`, reading the case count as N+1 (`table.labels.resize(operand+1)`) and the scrutinee register. `ReadTable()` reads the literal jump-target array from guest memory at the LIS/ADDI-computed base, applying the per-variant scale (word table vs byte-offset vs short-offset added to a base). Output is a TOML with `[[switch]]` entries: `base` (the bctr address), `r` (register), `default`, and a `labels = [0x..., ...]` array. The recompiler then turns a `bctr` that has a matching switch table into a real C++ `switch (r.u64){ case i: goto loc_XXXX; ... default: __builtin_unreachable(); }` instead of an indirect call.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the single most directly stealable algorithm for ps3recomp's 'indirect branches hard to resolve statically' gap. GCC/SN PS3 PPU compilers emit nearly identical switch idioms (lis/addi to form a table base, lwzx/lbzx/lhzx to load an entry, mtctr+bctr to jump), so the same opcode-mask + backward-cmplwi-scan + literal-table-read recipe applies with minimal change. Generating a side-channel TOML of resolved tables (instead of trying to resolve at lift time) lets the lifter emit real switch/goto and keeps the human able to hand-add tables the matcher misses. SPU has its own bisled/bi indirect branch with brhz/lqd-based dispatch tables — the same backward-scan-for-bound + read-literal-table approach can be ported to the SPU lifter.

dimensions.dimension: TOML config format (size hints, switch tables, hooks, optimization flags)
dimensions.howItWorks: The recompiler is driven entirely by a TOML config parsed into `RecompilerConfig`. Keys: [main] file_path / patch_file_path / patched_file_path / out_directory_path / switch_table_file_path (points at the analyse-generated table file). Optimization flags (default false): skip_lr, skip_msr, ctr_as_local, xer_as_local, reserved_as_local, cr_as_local, non_argument_as_local, non_volatile_as_local (each toggles whether that guest register lives in a C local vs the ctx struct). Save/restore helper addresses: restgprlr_14_address, savegprlr_14_address, restfpr_14_address, savefpr_14_address, restvmx_14_address, savevmx_14_address, restvmx_64_address, savevmx_64_address. longjmp_address / setjmp_address (redirected to native impls). `functions = [{address, size}]` for manual boundary override. `invalid_instructions = [{data, size}]` to skip non-code bytes (padding `0x00000000`, the C++ frame handler word, etc.). `[[midasm_hook]]` blocks: name, registers=["r3",...] (which guest regs to pass to the host hook), and the mutually-exclusive control keys return / return_on_true / return_on_false / jump_address / jump_address_on_true / jump_address_on_false / after_instruction. These map to RecompilerMidAsmHook {name, registers, ret, returnOnTrue, returnOnFalse, jumpAddress, jumpAddressOnTrue, jumpAddressOnFalse, afterInstruction} and RecompilerSwitchTable {r, labels[]}.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already uses Python scripts; adopting a single TOML/JSON config of the same shape would make per-title patching reproducible and reviewable. The most valuable items to copy: (1) explicit `functions=[{address,size}]` overrides to bridge the recall gap title-by-title; (2) `invalid_instructions`/data-region carve-outs (PS3 binaries interleave switch tables and literal pools that must not be lifted as code); (3) the mid-asm hook DSL — invaluable for the PS3 reality where you must patch around an un-lifted/un-HLE'd routine by injecting a native call at a specific guest PC with chosen registers and optional early-return/redirect; (4) the per-register localization flags are a portable performance lever once a title boots. The save/restore-helper and setjmp/longjmp address keys map onto PPC64 millicode and newlib setjmp/longjmp in PS3 ELFs.

dimensions.howItWorks: Defined in XenonUtils/ppc_context.h. Every register is a `union PPCRegister { s8/u8/s16/u16/s32/u32/s64/u64/f32/f64 }` so the same storage is reinterpreted per-instruction without casts. Vectors: `union alignas(0x10) PPCVRegister { s8[16]/u8[16]/s16[8]/u16[8]/s32[4]/u32[4]/s64[2]/u64[2]/f32[4]/f64[2] }`. Status regs are split into fields for cheap access: `PPCXERRegister {so,ov,ca}`, `PPCCRRegister {lt,gt,eq,so/un}` (8 of them, cr0..cr7, with templated compare() helpers), `PPCFPSCRRegister {uint32_t csr; getcsr()/setcsr() with platform RoundShift/RoundMask/FlushMask}` (the FPSCR is stored as the host MXCSR/FPCR-style control word so flush/round mode maps to hardware directly). `struct alignas(0x40) PPCContext` holds r0..r31, lr (uint64_t), ctr, xer, reserved (the load-reserved address for lwarx/stwcx), msr, cr0..cr7, fpscr, f0..f31, v0..v127 (note VMX128 has 128 vector regs vs base VMX's 32). Notably the struct is laid out with hot/argument registers (r3, r1, ...) first and non-volatiles grouped, and many fields are 'conditional' depending on optimization flags. PPC_FUNC(x) expands to `void x(PPCContext& __restrict ctx, uint8_t* base)`; PPC_FUNC_IMPL/extern "C" variants exist for the generated bodies.

vector register as a 10-way union incl. f32[4]/u8[16] for element-typed access
CR split into lt/gt/eq/so byte fields (branch tests are just field reads)
FPSCR stored as host control word (csr) so rounding/flush maps to MXCSR/FPCR
explicit `reserved` field to model lwarx/stwcx load-reservation
alignas(0x40) context + alignas(0x10) vectors for SIMD load/store
uniform PPC_FUNC signature (ctx&, base) with __restrict for aliasing freedom
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's ppu_context can copy this almost verbatim — the PS3 PPU is the same 64-bit PowerPC with the same GPRs/FPRs/CR/XER/CTR/LR/FPSCR and 32 VMX/AltiVec vector regs (use v0..v31, not 128). The union-per-register pattern eliminates a class of cast bugs in the lifter and lets each emitted instruction pick the right view (.u64/.s32/.f64). Storing FPSCR as the host control word is the clean way to get PPU rounding/denormal behavior. The explicit `reserved` field is the right model for PPU lwarx/ldarx/stwcx./stdcx. atomic reservations, which PS3 games use heavily for locks. For the SPU, build a parallel spu_context: 128 x 128-bit GPRs (single register file, all vector), the special channels, and 256KB local store as a flat array — the same union/alignas idioms apply.

dimensions.howItWorks: Recompiler::Recompile() is a large per-opcode switch (keyed on ppc_insn from an internal disassembler) where each case writes formatted C++ text via println()/print() (fmt-style). Operands are rendered through lambdas r()/f()/v()/cr()/ctr()/xer() that emit either `ctx.rN` or a bare local `rN` depending on the as_local flags, recording usage in RecompilerLocalVariables {ctr,xer,reserved,cr[8],r[32],f[32],v[128],env,temp,vTemp,ea}. Examples: ADD -> `{d}.u64 = {a}.u64 + {b}.u64;`; LWZ -> `{d}.u64 = PPC_LOAD_U32({base_reg}.u32 + {disp});`; MTLR/MFLR -> `ctx.lr = {r}.u64;` / `{r}.u64 = ctx.lr;` (elided if skip_lr); MTCTR -> `{ctr} = {r}.u64;`. Each generated function body is wrapped in PPC_FUNC_IMPL(__imp__NAME){ PPC_FUNC_PROLOGUE(); ... }. Local-variable declarations for the registers actually touched are emitted at the top. The output is deliberately NOT decompiled/readable — it is a faithful 1:1 transliteration so semantics match the hardware.
