XenonAnalyse .pdata exception-directory parse for exact bounds of stack-frame functions
branch-link scan + static length analysis for leaf/no-frame functions
TOML `functions` list of explicit (address,size) overrides
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This directly attacks ps3recomp's headline gap (72% recall, ~1000 functions Ghidra finds but find_functions.py misses because they are call-target-reachable, absent from .opd, or lack a standard prologue). Two transferable mechanisms: (1) PS3 PPU ELFs have a .pdata-equivalent — PRX/SELF PPC exception/unwind info and the .opd table give exact entry points and TOC for many functions; parse it the way XenonAnalyse parses .pdata before falling back to prologue scanning. (2) Adopt N64Recomp/splat's model where the boundary set is an EXTERNAL curated artifact, not a one-shot heuristic: emit a symbol_addrs-style file that merges find_functions.py output + Ghidra's call-target analysis + .opd + manual TOML overrides, so recall becomes a data problem you can iteratively close to 100% rather than an algorithm you must perfect.

dimensions.howItWorks: Both recompilers do deliberately LITERAL, low-complexity, instruction-by-instruction translation, one guest function -> one C/C++ function whose first argument is a CPU-state struct pointer (ctx). N64Recomp: `addiu $r4,$r4,0x20` becomes `ctx->r4 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0x20);`; every guest function emitted into its own file. XenonRecomp: every PPC function takes the ppc_context struct as arg1 and a base pointer as arg2 (Xbox 360 uses 32-bit guest pointers). No beautification — correctness over readability. Helper macros (ADD32, S32, RELOC_HI16, LOOKUP_FUNC) keep the emitted code small and push semantics into the runtime header.

literal per-instruction emission, no IR optimization (let the C compiler optimize)
macro-based semantics (ADD32, S32) so emitter stays tiny
base-pointer arg2 for 32-bit guest pointer worlds
per-function output files for incremental rebuild and patch-linking
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already mirrors this exactly (one C function per guest fn, ppu_context*/spu_context*). The transferable refinement is XenonRecomp's optimization config (below) and the macro discipline — and the SPU implication: ps3recomp can lift SPU functions the same literal way, but because SPU code is dynamically DMA'd into the 256KB local store, the SPU equivalent of LOOKUP_FUNC (resolve by local-store address at runtime) matters more than for the PPU.

dimensions.howItWorks: XenonRecomp maps most VMX/VMX128 instructions to x86 intrinsics, and uses the SIMD Everywhere (SIMDe) library to get an ARM64 backend for free. Two subtle correctness tricks: (1) big-endian vectors are handled by reversing the ENTIRE 16-byte vector rather than swapping per-element, so VMX instruction implementations must reference components in reversed order (it uses W,Z,Y instead of X,Y,Z); (2) floating-point denormal handling is toggled per-instruction-class inside ctx — VMX always flushes denormals to zero, while the scalar FPU must preserve them, so the recompiler flips the host FPU denormal/flush-to-zero mode around VMX vs FPU instruction groups.
techniques: VMX -> x86 intrinsics, SIMDe for ARM64 portability
reverse the whole 16-byte vector for big-endian, then swizzle component access (WZYX)
per-instruction-class denormal/flush-to-zero mode toggling in ctx
model FP control state as fields in the CPU context struct
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Highest-value direct transfer for the PPU lifter: PS3 PPU VMX/AltiVec is the SAME 128-bit ISA family as Xenon VMX128 (Xenon is the closest prior art). ps3recomp can copy XenonRecomp's intrinsic mapping table and its two correctness tricks wholesale: whole-vector byte reversal for big-endian load/store, and denormal-mode toggling between VMX and the scalar FPU. For SPU (custom 128-bit ISA, not VMX) the intrinsic-mapping APPROACH transfers (lower each SPU vector op to an x86/NEON intrinsic, model the 128 SPU registers as __m128 in spu_context) but the opcode tables must be authored fresh; SIMDe is still the right portability layer.

dimensions.howItWorks: DECOMP side sidesteps this: matching C re-expresses the original call as a normal C function pointer, so the boundary problem dissolves. RECOMP side has two complementary strategies. (1) N64Recomp: any unresolved `jalr $25` is emitted as `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r25)(rdram, ctx);` — the recompiler punts to runtime; the runtime keeps a table of which sections/overlays are loaded at which guest address and maps the guest address to the right recompiled C function pointer. (2) XenonRecomp: virtual/indirect calls go through a runtime 'perfect hash table' — dereferencing a 64-bit pointer indexed by (original_instruction_address * 2) yields the recompiled function's host address; the function-address array is placed just past the valid XEX memory region, with bounds exported as macros in ppc_config.h.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Directly addresses ps3recomp's 'indirect branches hard to resolve statically' gap. The lesson: do NOT try to resolve every indirect branch statically. Build a runtime guest-address-to-host-function map (a sorted table or perfect hash over all known entry points) and emit every unresolved bctr/bctrl/blr-through-register as a LOOKUP_FUNC-style runtime call. This makes recall of indirect targets a runtime concern, not a static-analysis blocker — so a game can boot with imperfect static analysis. For PS3 specifically: PPC vtables and switch tables, and SPU branch-indirect (bi/bisl), all funnel into the same runtime resolver. This is probably the single most important architectural change to let a game boot.

dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp does static jump-table recovery via register-state tracking: it keeps a RegState per register with prev_lui/prev_addiu_vram/prev_addend_reg and valid_* flags, and matches the sequence lui rt,hi -> addiu rt,rt,lo (forms rodata table base) -> addu (adds scaled index, exactly one operand must carry the valid lui, the other is the index reg) -> lw (loads target, base must be valid_lui+valid_addend) -> jr. On match it computes the table's rom address (vram + func.rom - func.vram), walks rodata in 4-byte steps reading each word, and validates each entry lies within the function range (jtbl_word >= func.vram && < func.vram+func.size); it stops at the first out-of-range word or the next table, and requires >=1 entry. Emits a real C switch with `L_{addr}` labels; bails to LOOKUP_FUNC on any pattern violation (e.g. consecutive addius, neither addu operand valid, zero entries). XenonRecomp detects the PPC idiom `mtctr r0` followed by `bctr` with preceding address-computation instructions, and XenonAnalyse writes detected tables to a separate switch_tables TOML that the recompiler reads to emit switch cases. Detection is acknowledged to be game-specific and may need tuning per title.

emit C switch with computed-address labels, fall back to LOOKUP_FUNC

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: PS3 PPU uses the same PowerPC mtctr/bctr table idiom XenonRecomp targets, so XenonAnalyse's detector is nearly drop-in for the PPU lifter (watch for TOC/.opd-relative table bases and r2-relative addressing instead of absolute). Two concrete steals: (1) the register-state-tracking algorithm from N64Recomp (track which reg holds the table base, bound the table by the enclosing function's range) generalizes to PPC and to SPU; (2) the pattern of EXTERNALIZING discovered tables into an editable TOML (switch_table_file_path) so a human can hand-correct the table base/entry-count when the heuristic fails — this turns the hardest static-analysis cases into a small data-entry task rather than a blocker, exactly what ps3recomp needs.

dimensions.howItWorks: The config files ARE the product. splat: a YAML where subsegments are `[rom_offset, type, name]` (types: asm, hasm (handwritten asm), c, data, rodata, bss, bin) or `{start:, type:, vram:}`; symbol_addrs_path points to curated symbol files; reloc_addrs_path overrides relocations; it emits a linker script with auto symbols like SEGMENT_VRAM_START/END. N64Recomp: a TOML with input/output paths, a `functions` boundary list, per-function `stub`/`skip` flags, single-instruction patches, and `[[patches.func]]`/`[[patches.hook]]` sections; a separate single-file patch output linked BEFORE the main output so the linker takes patched symbols first. XenonRecomp: TOML with [main] (file_path, patch_file_path, patched_file_path, out_directory_path, switch_table_file_path), register-save/restore stub addresses (restgprlr_14/savegprlr_14, restfpr_14, restvmx_14, restvmx_64 etc.), `functions`, `invalid_instructions` (32-bit values to skip — exception data/padding), `[[midasm_hook]]` (name/address/registers/return/jump_address/after_instruction), and optimization flags.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's pipeline (elf_parser.py -> find_functions.py -> lifters) should grow an equivalent externalized config layer so that everything the heuristics get wrong is human-correctable WITHOUT code changes: a TOML/YAML carrying manual PPU/SPU function boundaries, NID overrides, switch-table definitions, invalid-instruction ranges (PS3 ELFs have exception/unwind tables that look like code), and per-function stub/skip. The register-save/restore stub idea maps directly: PPC __savegpr/__restgpr/__savefpr/__savevmx milicode exist in PS3 binaries too and should be recognized as special. The mid-asm hook mechanism is how UnleashedRecomp injects PC enhancements — invaluable for ps3recomp modding. The patch-link-order trick gives ps3recomp a zero-decomp modding story.

dimensions.howItWorks: asm-processor lets a decomp keep functions it hasn't matched yet as raw assembly INSIDE the C file (GLOBAL_ASM(...) blocks) while still producing a byte-identical object. Mechanism: it replaces each GLOBAL_ASM block with a dummy C function/global sized to occupy the identical number of bytes the real asm will, compiles the C with the original (IDO) compiler, separately assembles the asm with GNU as, then overwrites the dummy sections in the object with the real assembled bytes, NOP-padding to keep symbol addresses valid so no relocation recomputation is needed. Its hardest job is 'late rodata': IDO emits read-only data in two passes (.rdata contents, then literals/jump tables into .late_rodata), so asm-processor emits matching dummy float/double/jumptable literals, assembles the true rodata separately, then relocates symbols/fixups into final position preserving alignment.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is about producing the symbol-rich ELF that a recompiler consumes, and about an incremental escape hatch. The transferable idea for ps3recomp: an asm-processor-like INCREMENTAL mode where functions the lifter can't yet handle (weird SPU dynamic loads, unresolved indirect-heavy functions) are left as a stub/interpreter-thunk while the rest is fully recompiled — i.e. graceful degradation per function rather than all-or-nothing, exactly matching N64Recomp's per-function stub/skip. Lower direct relevance because ps3recomp targets host-native C, not byte-matching, but the per-function fallback discipline is the takeaway.

dimensions.howItWorks: XenonRecomp memory-maps the executable's sections into a virtual address space mimicking the Xbox 360 layout, keeping the EXACT original memory layout so guest pointers stay valid; instruction implementations operate on little-endian values, so loads byte-swap on read and stores byte-swap before write, and all memory access is marked volatile to stop Clang from reordering. N64Recomp passes an rdram base + ctx to every function and resolves overlays at runtime via the section load-address table. Register-as-local optimization passes (ctr_as_local, xer_as_local, cr_as_local, non_volatile_as_local, non_argument_as_local, skip_lr) promote CPU-context fields to C locals where provably safe — reported ~20MB executable size reduction and multi-ms frame-time improvement.

The actionable steal is the OPTIMIZATION-FLAG layer: promote ppu_context fields (CR, XER, CTR, LR, non-volatile GPRs) to C locals within a function when no escape/indirect-call/exception forces a spill, configurable per-function via the TOML. Given PS3 binaries are large, the ~20MB/several-ms wins matter. Also adopt 'volatile at the memory boundary' to prevent MSVC/Clang from reordering big-endian swaps. setjmp/longjmp: PS3 libc uses them heavily; XenonRecomp's approach (redirect to native setjmp/longjmp via configured addresses, size ctx to hold host CPU state) is the template.

dimensions.howItWorks: The decomp ecosystem resolves OS/library calls by NAMING them in the symbol map: splat symbol_addrs lines give every libultra/OS function a human name and type:func, and matching decomp links against reimplemented libultra. Recompilers handle imports by stubbing: N64Recomp's TOML can `stub` or `skip` functions so the runtime supplies a hand-written native implementation; XenonRecomp leaves Xbox kernel imports / MMIO unimplemented and expects the runtime (UnleashedRecomp) to provide HLE. The boundary contract is again the symbol map: a name at an address tells the recompiler 'this is an import, don't lift it, call the HLE shim instead.'

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's NID layer (32-bit NID = SHA1(name)[:4], HLE libs) is the analogue of the decomp symbol map for imports. Transferable refinement: treat every resolved NID as a symbol_addrs/TOML entry of type 'import' so the lifter automatically STUBS it (emit a call to the HLE shim, never lift the PRX body) — and conversely flag unresolved NIDs as auto-stub-with-warning so missing HLE doesn't block a boot. The stub/skip TOML mechanism is exactly how ps3recomp should let cellVdec/cellAdec/cellGcmSys be progressively filled: stub now, implement later, per-function, data-driven.

dimensions.howItWorks: Neither decomp ports nor these recompilers translate GPU microcode the way they translate CPU code; they HLE the graphics API. Decomp/recomp N64 ports pair with RT64 (an external N64 GPU renderer) and feed it via the recompiled game calling the HLE'd graphics-API functions; XenonRecomp pairs with XenosRecomp which separately recompiles Xenos SHADERS into HLSL (not the FIFO/command processor — that is reimplemented). So the command-processor/FIFO layer is always HLE/reimplemented, and only the programmable shaders are 'recompiled.'

The one transferable idea is XenosRecomp: RSX fragment/vertex programs are themselves a compiled ISA (NV shader microcode); a separate 'RsxShaderRecomp' that translates RSX shader microcode -> SPIR-V/HLSL is a cleaner long-term path than interpreting shaders. The mid-asm-hook pattern is how to inject widescreen/HUD/aspect fixes at specific cellGcm call sites.

dimensions.howItWorks: The standout finding: recomp and decomp are a PIPELINE, not alternatives. (1) N64Recomp's required input is an ELF whose symbol/boundary/relocation metadata is produced by the decomp toolchain (splat+spimdisasm) — the decomp's curated symbol_addrs IS the recompiler's function table. (2) Zelda64Recomp reuses the decompilation project's HEADERS, STRUCTS, and named FUNCTIONS to write mods and enhancements, even though the port itself is recompiled, not decompiled. Wiseguy: recomp needs far less per-game RE ('understanding where code is in the ROM', ~2 days for Superman) than full decomp, yet its patching system makes modifying the game 'almost as easy as directly modifying the decompilation.' So: decomp supplies recall + semantics (symbols/structs), recomp supplies the cheap path to a running native binary.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the strategic blueprint for closing ps3recomp's 72%-recall gap and reaching a boot. Concretely: (1) Make the boundary/symbol set an EXTERNAL curated artifact (a splat-style symbol_addrs + TOML) that merges find_functions.py + Ghidra call-target analysis + .opd + manual additions; recall then improves by adding data, not rewriting heuristics. (2) Where a PS3 decomp or partial RE exists (or Ghidra-exported symbols), feed those names/structs straight into the lifter as the metadata contract — exactly N64Recomp's ELF-in model. (3) Reuse any decomp-derived struct/header knowledge for HLE and for mods. (4) For SPU dynamic-load and indirect-heavy code that static analysis can't reach, lean on the runtime resolver (LOOKUP_FUNC by guest/local-store address) so the game boots with imperfect static recall and you backfill symbols over time.

standoutInnovations: LOOKUP_FUNC runtime indirection: don't resolve indirect calls statically — emit LOOKUP_FUNC(guest_addr)(ctx) and let a runtime guest-address->host-function table resolve it, so a game can boot despite imperfect static analysis (directly fixes ps3recomp's indirect-branch and SPU-dynamic-load blockers).

Externalize every hard case into an editable config: switch tables (switch_table_file_path TOML), function boundaries (functions list), invalid-instruction ranges, NID/import names — turning unsolvable static-analysis problems into small human data-entry tasks.

The symbol map is the universal contract: a curated `name = 0xADDR; // type:func size: rom:` artifact is BOTH the decomp's source of truth AND the recompiler's required input — so recall becomes a data problem that converges to 100%, not an algorithm to perfect.

Whole-16-byte vector reversal (not per-element) plus per-instruction-class denormal/flush-to-zero toggling — XenonRecomp's two big-endian-VMX correctness tricks, copyable wholesale to the PS3 PPU AltiVec lifter since Xenon VMX128 is the same ISA family.

Register-as-local optimization passes (non_volatile_as_local, ctr/xer/cr_as_local, skip_lr) gated by per-function safety flags: promote CPU-context fields to C locals where provably safe, reported ~20MB binary shrink and multi-ms frame-time gains.

XenonAnalyse using the .pdata exception/unwind directory to get exact function boundaries for free for every stack-frame function — PS3 PPC ELFs have the analogous .opd + unwind tables, a near-free recall boost over prologue scanning.

Patch-link-order trick: compile changed functions into a separate object linked BEFORE the base output so the linker prefers patched symbols — gives a zero-decomp modding/hotfix story on a recompiled binary.

asm-processor's per-function escape hatch (GLOBAL_ASM): keep not-yet-handled functions as raw asm/stubs inside an otherwise fully-built binary — the graceful per-function degradation model ps3recomp should adopt instead of all-or-nothing.

XenosRecomp recompiles only the programmable shaders (Xenos microcode -> HLSL) while the command processor is reimplemented/HLE'd — validating that ps3recomp should HLE the RSX FIFO but could separately recompile RSX shader microcode to SPIR-V.
verifiableClaims: XenonAnalyse derives exact function boundaries from the XEX .pdata exception-directory segment for functions with stack allocation, and falls back to branch-link scanning + static length analysis plus a TOML `functions` override for the rest.

XenonRecomp handles big-endian VMX vectors by reversing the entire 16-byte vector (not swapping individual 32-bit elements), which forces component access in reversed order (e.g. W,Z,Y instead of X,Y,Z), and toggles FPU denormal flush-to-zero per instruction class (VMX flushes, scalar FPU preserves).

N64Recomp emits unresolved indirect calls such as `jalr $25` as `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r25)(rdram, ctx);`, delegating resolution to a runtime that maps loaded section/overlay addresses to recompiled functions; it statically recovers jump tables via per-register RegState tracking of the lui->addiu->addu->lw->jr pattern, bounding entries to the enclosing function's vram range.

N64Recomp requires an ELF symbol table (typically produced by a splat/spimdisasm disassembly or decompilation setup) as its function-boundary/name/relocation metadata source, and Zelda64Recomp reuses decompilation-project headers/structs/function symbols for mods and enhancements — establishing decomp->recomp as a pipeline.

asm-processor achieves byte-matching by replacing GLOBAL_ASM blocks with size-identical dummy C placeholders, compiling with the original (IDO) compiler, then overwriting those sections with separately-assembled machine code and NOP-padding to keep symbol addresses valid, with special two-pass handling for IDO's .late_rodata (literals + jump tables).

research.project: Static binary translation theory: function-boundary and indirect-branch recovery (survey of techniques applicable to ps3recomp's PPU/SPU/RSX/HLE pipeline)
research.summary: ps3recomp's two biggest static-analysis gaps — ~72% function-detection recall and unresolved indirect branches (function pointers, vtables, switch tables) — are exactly the problems that the academic/industrial SBT literature has spent two decades attacking, and the methods cluster into a few transferable families. For function boundaries, the highest-leverage shift is from prologue/signature scanning (which fails on optimized hand-written code, the same failure ps3recomp hits) toward CFG-structural detection: Nucleus builds an interprocedural CFG, hides call edges, and uses weakly-connected-components + "block has no incoming intraprocedural edge" to recover entries with no prologue at F-score ~0.95; rev.ng formalizes a 5-step candidate-function-entry-point (CFEP) algorithm with an explicit keep/discard rule (kept only if reachable solely via calls or skipping-jumps) plus killer-basic-block noreturn detection. For indirect branches, three independent works (rev.ng OSRA, ddisasm register-value analysis, SJA) converge on the same affine abstract domain base + index*mult + disp computed only along def-use chains feeding the jump, with SJA's 2024 advance being a forward, all-paths, soundness-preserving analysis that relates the index variable to the target (where classic VSA collapses to ⊤ on the table memory read) and an equality-equivalence-class bounds analysis to recover table size even when the bound check is on a different variable. Crucially for PS3, both prior PS3-era prior art (XenonRecomp for the same PowerPC+VMX PPU) and emulators (RPCS3) accept that pure static recovery is incomplete and lean on a TOML feedback file of manual function/switch overrides plus a runtime perfect-hash dispatch table mapping guest address -> recompiled function, which is the most directly copyable mechanism. The PowerPC ELFv1 .opd/TOC descriptor structure (3 doublewords: entry, r2/TOC, env) is both a high-recall function-entry oracle ps3recomp can mine and a correctness constraint the lifter must model. Confidence-scored detection (ddisasm's weighted-evidence Datalog aggregation; ML disassemblers XDA/DeepDi) and Ghidra Function ID (dual full/specific hashes + call-tree disambiguation) round out practical recall boosters.

dimensions.howItWorks: Nucleus (Andriesse et al., EuroS&P 2017) abandons prologue/epilogue signatures entirely. It linearly disassembles, builds an Interprocedural CFG (ICFG) digraph G=(V,E) of all basic blocks with both intra- and inter-procedural edges, then: (1) hides all call edges E_call; (2) finds directly-called entry blocks via a pass for direct call targets and expands each into a function by following remaining edges (undirected) until a weakly-connected component closes; (3) for blocks still unassigned (indirectly-called / unreachable functions), runs weakly-connected-components and detects entry points as basic blocks with NO incoming intraprocedural edge; loopback-into-entry is disambiguated because loopbacks target an offset *inside* the block (past the prologue) rather than its start, and via intraprocedural loop detection. Last-resort entry = lowest address. Core insight: intraprocedural control flow uses structurally different edge patterns than interprocedural, and this holds across compilers/opt-levels, so it needs zero compiler-specific heuristics. ICFG+detection is only ~850 SLOC. Mean F-score 0.95; nearly all false positives trace to UNresolved intraprocedural switch edges leaving isolated case blocks (so better switch recovery directly raises function recall). To avoid merging a tail-callee into its caller, directly-called blocks are expanded *directed* (don't follow inbound edges into a known direct-call entry).

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Directly attacks ps3recomp's ~72% recall problem: the ~1000 functions Ghidra finds 'by call-target analysis, not in .opd, no standard prologue' are exactly Nucleus's indirectly-called/no-prologue case. find_functions.py should build a PPU ICFG (bl=call edge, b/bc=intra edge, bctr/blr=indirect/return) and run connected-components rather than prologue matching. Because Nucleus is architecture-agnostic and CFG-level, it ports to PowerPC and to SPU (br/brsl=call-ish, bi/bisl=indirect). The finding that switch-edge gaps cause the false positives tells ps3recomp that fixing jump-table recovery and function recall are the same problem.

dimensions.dimension: Candidate-function-entry-point (CFEP) algorithm with keep/discard rule + tail-call handling
dimensions.howItWorks: rev.ng (Di Federico et al., CC 2017) recovers function boundaries in 5 steps on an accurate CFG: (1) Identify calls/returns ISA-agnostically — a *call* = a branch preceded by a store of a constant integer equal to the next PC (the return address); a *return* = an indirect branch whose targets are unknown or are known return addresses (captures lr-saving PowerPC/ARM and stack-saving x86 uniformly). (2) Build initial CFEP set from three sources: (a) called targets (most reliable), (b) UNUSED intervals of global data (function pointers / C++ vtables), explicitly blacklisting any global-data bytes SET already read as jump-table entries to suppress false positives, (c) in-code constants that never flow into PC and are never used as a load address. (3) For each CFEP follow CFG without entering calls (jump to return addr) and stopping at returns, recording how each block was reached, and detect 'skipping jumps' (a jump that hops over a type-(a) CFEP — a tail-call hint). (4) Filter: keep a CFEP iff it is reachable ONLY through call instructions or skipping-jumps; discard CFEPs reachable through another function's local CFG (fallthrough/return paths) since that means two functions share a body, not a tail call. (5) Finalize: promote surviving jumps to calls and recompute reachable blocks (functions may legitimately share code). Noreturn detection (paramount to avoid merging the function after a call into the caller): mark 'killer basic blocks' for syscall wrappers writing a noreturn syscall id (e.g. exit), infinite loops (abort), and longjmp (stack pointer overwritten by a value not derived as sp±offset or load(sp±k)); then everything post-dominated by the sink becomes noreturn.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: The keep/discard rule is a concrete recipe ps3recomp can implement to add the missing ~1000 functions without the false positives that naive call-target scraping produces. The noreturn handling maps to PS3 directly: sys_process_exit / abort / longjmp on PPU otherwise cause the next function to be swallowed into the caller (a boundary bug). The 'unused global data interval' source mines PPU function pointers and C++ vtables; combined with .opd mining it is a strong recall source. SPU has no lr-store convention identical to PPU but brsl writes the return PC to a GPR, fitting the 'store of next PC' call definition.

dimensions.dimension: Indirect-branch / jump-table target recovery via affine value analysis (the shared core)
dimensions.howItWorks: Three independent systems converge on the SAME abstract domain — a value is (base register/const) + index*multiplier + displacement, tracked ONLY along the def-use chain that feeds the indirect branch: (1) rev.ng SET (Simple Expression Tracker) walks backward from a store-to-PC, pushing single-non-constant-operand ops onto a stack until a constant is hit, then replays the stack to materialize the value; it can follow memory loads from global data (reading the program image) to materialize jump-table contents. OSRA (Offset Shape and Range Analysis) tracks values as a+b*x with x in [c,d]; bounds come from constant comparisons on conditional branches, signedness inferred from signed/unsigned op usage. When SET hits a load OSRA can't model, it enumerates the OSRA-bounded index values, performs the loads, and produces all PC targets. rev.ng adds reaching-definition extensions: OSR merging across multiple reaching defs (only if multiplying factors match), path-sensitive merging (Algorithm 1, DFS over predecessors, used as fallback), and Condition Numbering Analysis (CNA) that hashes branch conditions so a predicated def isn't spuriously propagated past a guard sharing its predicate. (2) ddisasm (Datalog Disassembly, USENIX Sec 2020) computes def_used chains, then def_used_for_address (backward-transitive from memory-access instructions), then reg_val(A,Reg,A2,Reg2,Mult,Disp) — literally base+index*mult+disp — only for address-computing registers, for scalability. (3) SJA (Static Jump Table Analysis, ISSTA 2024) is the modern advance: a purely FORWARD, all-paths, SOUNDNESS-preserving abstract interpretation whose domain relates the INDEX variable to the target (recursive domain handles 4 jump-table forms incl. multi-level nested). Key argument vs VSA: VSA computes the set of possible *values* but on the table memory-read it unions table contents and collapses to ⊤, losing the index↔target relation; SJA keeps the relation symbolic and never collapses. SJA's bounds analysis recovers table size via equality-equivalence classes (x = a*y + b put y and x in one class through an injected representative), so it can infer the index bound even when the explicit bound check is on a DIFFERENT but equality-related variable — handling the 'x=y; if(y<5)' case rev.ng/OSRA miss. SJA runs at ~300 KB/s, O(I*V), 35x fewer misses than prior work, 2% FP. Iterates: each newly discovered target adds reachable code that may contain more tables (n-level nesting => n iterations).

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the core fix for ps3recomp's switch-table / indirect-branch gap on BOTH PPU and SPU. PPU switch idiom: the bctr (jump to CTR) preceded by an address computed as table_base + index*4 (or rldicr/rlwinm scaling) — exactly the affine domain. ps3recomp should slice backward from each bctr/bctrl over GPR def-use, recover base/mult/disp, recover the index bound (SJA-style, since PPU often bounds via a separate cmplwi on a related reg), read the in-image table, and emit a real C switch. SJA's soundness emphasis matters because a recompiler that misses a target produces a wrong binary, not just an imprecise analysis. The same slice resolves SPU bi/bisl jump tables in local store. rev.ng's blacklisting of table bytes also feeds the function-boundary pass (don't treat table entries as vtable function pointers).

dimensions.dimension: PowerPC ELFv1 .opd function descriptors and TOC (r2) — PS3-specific entry oracle + correctness constraint
dimensions.howItWorks: PS3 PPU uses the 64-bit PowerPC ELFv1 ABI. Every externally-visible function has a 3-doubleword descriptor in the .opd (Official Procedure Descriptor) section: [0]=function entry-point address, [1]=TOC base (the r2 value for that function), [2]=environment pointer (0 for C/C++). Critically, a function symbol's st_value is the address of the DESCRIPTOR, not the code — so naive symbol-as-entry logic lands on .opd data, not code. Calls are R_PPC64_REL24 relocations resolved to the real entry; call sites are 'bl target; nop' where the nop becomes 'ld r2,40(r1)' to restore the caller's TOC for preemptible/cross-module calls. r2 is call-preserved and set by the caller in ELFv1 (vs callee in ELFv2). Function pointers in C source are therefore pointers to descriptors, and an indirect call must load both the entry and the new r2 from the descriptor.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already parses ELF but should treat .opd as a near-100%-recall oracle for exported/visible function entries — every descriptor's doubleword[0] is a guaranteed entry. The gap (functions 'not in .opd') is precisely the un-exported/static functions Nucleus/rev.ng/CFEP must recover by CFG analysis, so .opd-mining + CFG-structural detection are complementary and together should close most of the 28% recall gap. The TOC angle is also a correctness item: the runtime/lifter must model r2 per function (each guest function's r2 base) so that TOC-relative loads of global data resolve; indirect-call lowering through function pointers must read the descriptor, and ps3recomp's perfect-hash dispatch must key on the descriptor entry address.

dimensions.dimension: Runtime fallback for unresolvable indirect calls (perfect-hash / dispatch table)
dimensions.howItWorks: When static recovery cannot enumerate an indirect call/jump target (function pointers, virtual calls, computed branches), all production recompilers/translators keep a runtime guest-PC -> host-function map. XenonRecomp (the closest prior art — same PowerPC+VMX128 PPU as PS3's PPU) lowers every indirect call through a perfect-hash table: it dereferences a 64-bit pointer at (original_instruction_address * 2) to get the recompiled function address; valid pointer regions are emitted as macros in ppc_config.h and the function-pointer table is placed after the valid XEX memory region. Dynamic binary translators generalize this as an IBTC (indirect branch target cache) / software dispatch with inline caching (Tiaozhuan, BT works) keyed on source PC. The recompiler emits a call to a dispatch helper that looks up the translated block for the current guest address and chains to it (with block linking to elide repeat dispatch).

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the single most directly copyable mechanism for ps3recomp because XenonRecomp is the same PPU ISA family. ps3recomp's runtime (host_ptr = g_base + guest_addr) already has guest addresses; it should build a guest_addr -> recompiled_fn table covering all detected functions and route any unresolved bctrl/bctr/bisl through it. This makes 100% static indirect-target recovery unnecessary for booting: missed targets degrade to a runtime lookup instead of a wrong binary. It also handles RSX/SPU function pointers passed across the HLE boundary and dynamically-loaded SPU code (whose entry is only known at DMA time).

dimensions.dimension: Frontend-as-oracle / IDA-Ghidra feedback loop + TOML override config
dimensions.howItWorks: McSema does NOT recover the CFG itself — it consumes a CFG protobuf produced by an IDA Pro (or Binary Ninja) frontend script, explicitly accepting 'McSema's CFG recovery depends on IDA Pro being accurate; sometimes it's not.' Indirect-call/jump-target quality is inherited from the disassembler. XenonRecomp formalizes a human-in-the-loop override: XenonAnalyse emits a TOML of detected functions and switch tables; the user supplements a main TOML with explicit boundaries `functions = [{address=0x..., size=0x...}]` (used 'when automatic analysis fails, particularly for jump-table-containing functions'), `invalid_instructions = [{data=0x..., size=4}]` to skip padding/exception-handler bytes, a separate `switch_table_file_path` (e.g. SWA_switch_tables.toml) consumed at LoadConfig, and `[[midasm_hook]]` blocks (name/address/registers/return/jump_address[_on_true/false]/after_instruction) for surgical patches. Register save/restore stubs (restgprlr_14, savevmx_64, setjmp/longjmp) are declared by address. Ghidra Function ID is the library-recognition oracle: per function it stores a 64-bit FULL hash (mnemonic + addressing-mode + register operands, but NOT constant-operand values and NOT calls/NOPs — so it's relocation-invariant) and a 64-bit SPECIFIC hash (full + constant values when heuristically non-address); matches need an instruction-count threshold; ambiguous identical bodies are disambiguated by hashing called child functions (parent/child relation), with Force-Specific / Force-Relation / Auto-Fail / Auto-Pass overrides.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's pipeline already has elf_parser.py + find_functions.py; the actionable lesson is (a) treat Ghidra as an authoritative function-list oracle and ingest its boundaries (Ghidra already finds the ~1000 functions ps3recomp misses), and (b) adopt a XenonRecomp-style TOML override layer so per-title manual fixes (function {address,size}, switch tables, invalid_instructions, midasm hooks) are first-class and reproducible — essential while no game boots end-to-end. Ghidra FID could identify statically-linked PS3 SDK / libc / Newlib routines on PPU and SPU, letting ps3recomp swap them for HLE or known-good implementations and shrink the lift surface. The relocation-invariant hashing handles PS3's PRX relocation.

dimensions.dimension: Confidence-scored / probabilistic boundary detection (weighted-evidence aggregation + ML)
dimensions.howItWorks: ddisasm reframes disassembly as weighted decisions in Datalog (Souffle). It over-approximates by superset-style traversal: encode every byte as data_byte(A,Val) and every 8-byte sequence that lands in a section as address_in_data(A,Addr) — making ALL jump-table entries and function pointers in data automatic traversal seeds (initial_target also includes entry points, function symbols, exception landing pads, section starts). It detects symbol-difference jump tables (Symbol1-Symbol2, common in PIC/ICC) with ad-hoc rules. Block conflicts (overlapping candidate blocks) are resolved by emitting block_points(Block,Src,Points,Why) facts from many heuristics (e.g. +points: block is called/jumped by a non-overlapping block; -points: a jump table overlaps the block), summing via Souffle aggregates, and discarding the lower-scored block / those below a threshold — exactly a confidence score. ML disassemblers push this further: XDA pretrains a 12-layer/12-head transformer on raw bytes (masked-byte LM) then fine-tunes for instruction- and function-boundary tasks (learning prologue/epilogue patterns like sub rsp / add rsp as soft signals); DeepDi does superset disassembly, builds an Instruction Flow Graph, and runs a Relational GCN to propagate per-instruction embeddings and classify true instructions/boundaries fast. Probabilistic Disassembly assigns each offset a probability of being an instruction start from register define-use, control-flow convergence, and control-flow crossing.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp can adopt the confidence model without ML: gather every boundary signal it already has (.opd entries=very high; direct bl targets=high; in-data 8-byte values pointing into .text=medium; no-prologue CFG entry=medium; prologue match=low-but-positive), assign weights, and resolve overlaps/conflicts by score instead of all-or-nothing — turning the binary 'found/not-found' into a ranked recall mechanism, and emitting a low-confidence list for the TOML reviewer. The address_in_data trick is a cheap recall booster for PPU function pointers/vtables and .opd descriptors. ML disassemblers (XDA/DeepDi) are inspirational: a PowerPC-trained model could pre-seed candidate entries, but training data and PPC support are the barrier, so this is a longer-term option than the rule-based scoring.

dimensions.dimension: SPU dynamically-loaded code (256KB local store overlays)
dimensions.howItWorks: ps3recomp's hardest static gap is SPU code DMA'd into local store at runtime — the entry/content isn't in the ELF statically. RPCS3 (the reference PS3 emulator) sidesteps this dynamically: an SPUAnalyser performs static analysis on each SPU program already resident in local store to find function boundaries and register usage before recompiling (ASMJIT for tight SIMD loops; LLVM for function-level optimization). Because the same overlay code can be DMA'd to different addresses, RPCS3 keys/caches compiled SPU blocks by the local-store CONTENTS (a hash of the instruction bytes of the discovered region) rather than by absolute address, so re-loaded overlays hit the cache. Block linking directly connects compiled blocks to avoid dispatch overhead; known indirect-branch targets are promoted to function-call targets; unknown targets fall back to dispatch/interpreter. RPCS3 also added precompilation (analyze/compile SPU programs ahead of first execution). The discovery itself is recursive traversal from the SPU entry following br/brsl (direct) and stopping/forking at bi/bisl (indirect) and bi $lr (return).

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: A purely-static AOT recompiler genuinely cannot enumerate SPU overlays ahead of time, so the transferable lesson is hybrid: ps3recomp should (a) statically lift every SPU code region it CAN find (in-image SPU ELFs / embedded modules) with the same affine jump-table + CFG recovery used for PPU, and (b) for code that only appears in local store at runtime, adopt RPCS3's content-hash-keyed cache so a guest DMA of an overlay triggers either a precompiled lift (matched by hash) or a fallback (interpret / JIT). This makes the SPU local-store DMA path a cache lookup on instruction-bytes hash rather than an unsolved static problem, and the same guest-PC dispatch table used for PPU indirect calls covers SPU bi/bisl.

standoutInnovations: Nucleus's edge-classification insight: hide call edges, then weakly-connected-components + 'no incoming intraprocedural edge = function entry' recovers no-prologue/indirectly-called functions with ZERO compiler-specific heuristics (F~0.95) — and its false positives are almost entirely unresolved switch edges, proving function recall and jump-table recovery are the same problem.

rev.ng's keep/discard CFEP rule: keep a candidate entry iff it is reachable ONLY through calls or skipping-jumps; discard if reachable through another function's local CFG — a one-line criterion that cleanly separates true tail-call entries from shared-code fragments and from jump-table case blocks.

The convergent affine domain base+index*mult+disp computed ONLY along the def-use slice feeding the indirect branch — independently arrived at by rev.ng OSRA, ddisasm reg_val, and SJA — is the canonical jump-table recovery primitive and is cheap enough to scale (ddisasm/SJA ~300KB/s).

SJA's index-to-target relational domain (vs VSA collapsing to ⊤ on the table memory read) + equality-equivalence-class bounds analysis that recovers table size even when the bound check is on a DIFFERENT but equality-related variable — 35x fewer missed targets while staying sound.

rev.ng's killer-basic-block noreturn detection (syscall-id write to exit/abort/longjmp via SP-overwrite, then post-dominator propagation) prevents the classic boundary bug of merging the post-call function into the caller — directly relevant to PS3 sys_process_exit/longjmp.

XenonRecomp's address*2 perfect-hash dispatch table for indirect calls on the SAME PowerPC+VMX ISA family — a drop-in runtime fallback that makes 100% static indirect-target recovery unnecessary for booting.

ddisasm's address_in_data superset seeding (every in-section 8-byte value that points into a section becomes a traversal target) plus weighted block_points conflict resolution via Datalog aggregates — turns recall into a tunable confidence score.

RPCS3's content-hash keying of compiled SPU regions so the same overlay DMA'd to different local-store addresses reuses one compilation — the practical answer to statically-invisible SPU dynamic loading.
verifiableClaims: Nucleus achieves a mean F-score of 0.95 (SPEC ~0.96) for function detection across gcc/clang/Visual Studio on x86/x64 at O0-O3 using only ICFG connected-components analysis with no compiler-specific signatures, and its ICFG+detection core is under 850 SLOC (Andriesse et al., EuroS&P 2017).

rev.ng defines a function call architecture-agnostically as a branch preceded by a store of a constant integer equal to the next PC (the return address) and a return as an indirect branch whose targets are unknown or known return addresses, and keeps a candidate function entry point iff it is reachable exclusively through call instructions or skipping-jumps (Di Federico et al., CC 2017).

SJA (ISSTA 2024) is a purely forward, all-paths, soundness-preserving jump-table analysis that relates the index variable to the jump target (where VSA collapses to top on the table memory read), recovers table bounds via equality-equivalence classes, runs at ~300 KB/s in O(I*V), and reports ~35x fewer missed targets and ~2% false positives versus prior tools (angr/Ghidra/Dyninst/Ddisasm).

PowerPC 64-bit ELFv1 (the PS3 PPU ABI) stores a 3-doubleword function descriptor per externally-visible function in .opd = {entry-point address, TOC/r2 base, environment pointer (0 for C/C++)}, and a function symbol's st_value is the address of the descriptor, not the code entry.

XenonRecomp resolves indirect calls at runtime by dereferencing a 64-bit pointer computed from (original instruction address * 2) in a perfect-hash table, and accepts manual TOML overrides including functions=[{address,size}], a separate switch_table_file_path, invalid_instructions=[{data,size}], and [[midasm_hook]] blocks; XenonAnalyse detects PPC jump tables by locating mtctr followed by bctr.

Ghidra Function ID stores two 64-bit hashes per function — a full hash (mnemonic + addressing mode + register operands, excluding constant-operand values and excluding call/NOP instructions, making it relocation-invariant) and a specific hash (adding non-address constant values) — and disambiguates identical bodies by hashing called child functions, gated by an instruction-count threshold.

research.project: RPCS3 SPU recompilation/HLE (SPU LLVM + ASMJIT, SPURS) and prior-art static recompilers (XenonRecomp/XenosRecomp, N64Recomp); plus clarification of the "Dusk" port
research.summary: RPCS3 emulates the Cell's SPUs with a per-SPU-context model (256KB local store as a flat byte array, 128 vector regs, channel-based I/O) plus two recompiler backends: an ASMJIT backend that emits x86 directly (good for tight homogeneous SIMD loops) and an LLVM backend that lowers SPU ops to LLVM IR (better float-semantics control and cross-arch via SIMD Everywhere on ARM64). A static SPUAnalyser pass finds function boundaries, splits blocks, analyzes register liveness, and classifies indirect branches before codegen. Crucially for ps3recomp, SPU code is compiled lazily at runtime keyed by the *content* of local store (functions hashed; SHA-1 over image segments on deploy), so dynamically DMA'd-in SPU images are handled by JIT-on-first-execution and cached to disk (Spu-*-v3/v4.dat); the absolute-addressing problem (e.g. Red Dead Redemption loading the same code to different LS addresses) is what defeats naive caching. SPURS is done as HLE: cellSpurs is reimplemented in C++ on the PPU side (CellSpurs/CellSpursTaskset/CellSpursJobChain structs, PPU "handler" threads, LV2 syscalls and event queues) rather than running Sony's real SPU kernel image. The closest static-recompilation prior art is hedge-dev's XenonRecomp (Xbox 360 PowerPC -> C++), which shares ps3recomp's exact problems (PowerPC+VMX, big-endian, function detection, indirect branches) and solves them with .pdata-driven boundaries, TOML jump-table/config files, a perfect-hash indirect-call table, and mid-asm hooks. The user's "Dusk" reference is NOT a static recompiler: it is the Twilight Princess GameCube native PC port (renamed Dusklight), built on the zeldaret/tp hand-decompilation, so it offers little to a recompiler beyond a portability-layer pattern (its Aurora framework).

dimensions.howItWorks: RPCS3 has two SPU JIT backends sharing a frontend analysis. ASMJIT (SPUASMJITRecompiler.cpp) emits x86-64 directly from a per-instruction template library without an IR, which suits SPU's tight, homogeneous 128-bit SIMD loops. The LLVM backend (SPULLVMRecompiler.cpp) lowers each SPU op to LLVM IR and lets LLVM's optimizer/backend produce native code; this is what enables ARM64 support (vector intrinsics via SIMD Everywhere) and lets RPCS3 'adjust' x86 float handling to match the SPU's non-IEEE single-precision quirks (extended-range, flush-to-zero, no NaN-propagation guarantees) for both accuracy and speed. Loads/stores to local store are marked volatile to block unsafe reordering. SPU local store is a 256KB host byte array indexed directly; 128 vector registers live in the spu_thread context struct.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's spu_lifter.py emits one C function per guest SPU function over an spu_context*. RPCS3 shows: (1) keep LS as a flat host array indexed by 18-bit LS address, (2) emit the SPU's odd float semantics explicitly (do NOT trust host IEEE), and (3) prefer emitting host SIMD intrinsics (SSE/AVX/NEON) rather than scalarizing the 128-bit ISA. For an AOT C path, the LLVM-style 'normalize the IR then let the C compiler optimize' is exactly what ps3recomp already does by emitting C; the key transferable lesson is correctness of float/saturation/rotate edge cases, not the JIT vs AOT split.

dimensions.howItWorks: Before codegen, a static SPUAnalyser pass walks the SPU image to identify function boundaries, split into basic blocks, analyze register usage/liveness (so dead vector regs aren't materialized), and classify control flow. Indirect branches (bi/bisl/bisled) are special-cased: known indirect-branch targets can be promoted to function-call targets; the analyser checks a 'stack mirror' structure first to resolve return targets (mirroring the LLVM backend), and BISLED is handled by separating the branch target from event flags. 'SPU block size' modes (Safe/Mega/Giga) control how aggressively small units are merged into larger compiled chunks (bigger = fewer dispatch round-trips, more code).

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Directly addresses two stated ps3recomp gaps: ~72% function recall and hard indirect branches. The 'stack mirror' (a shadow of the SPU stack to recover return addresses) is a concrete trick ps3recomp could add for SPU returns. The Safe/Mega/Giga block-merging knob is a config-format idea: let the toolkit emit either many small C functions or fused superblocks. For recall, RPCS3 reaches functions via call-target/branch analysis (same insight ps3recomp's docs note Ghidra uses) rather than relying on a symbol table.

dimensions.dimension: Dynamically-loaded SPU code (the core ps3recomp blocker)
dimensions.howItWorks: SPU programs are routinely DMA'd into local store at runtime, so they cannot all be found statically. RPCS3 sidesteps this by compiling lazily at *execution time*, keyed by the actual bytes in local store: when execution reaches an un-compiled region, the analyser hashes the function/block and either reuses a cached compilation or compiles fresh. sys_spu_image::deploy() computes a SHA-1 over image segments (COPY/FILL/INFO segment types) and applies patch_engine patches at load. Compiled SPU programs are cached to disk (Spu-<...>-v3/v4.dat) and meant to be reloaded next launch. A documented failure mode: titles like Red Dead Redemption use absolute addressing and load the *same* SPU code to *different* LS addresses, so address-keyed caching mismatches and the recompiler endlessly re-compiles — the fix is to key on content, not load address.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the single most important transferable mechanism. ps3recomp is pure AOT, but dynamically-loaded SPU images defeat any static-only pipeline. The practical answer is a hybrid: AOT-recompile all SPU images findable in the SELF/PRX/.opd, but also ship a runtime fallback that, on a cache miss, hashes the LS region and either (a) dispatches to an AOT C function pre-keyed by the same content hash, or (b) invokes a lightweight runtime translator/interpreter. Build a content-addressed table at recompile time: hash each known SPU image's bytes -> entrypoint into the compiled C. The RDR absolute-addressing caveat means ps3recomp should normalize/relocate before hashing, and must support the same image appearing at multiple LS base addresses.

dimensions.howItWorks: All SPU I/O goes through numbered channels modeled by two C++ classes: spu_channel (1-entry, atomic u64 = 32-bit value + flags; used for out_mbox, out_intr_mbox, events, tag updates; methods try_push/push/push_wait) and spu_channel_4_t (4-entry queue for the inbound mailbox). Named channels include SPU_RdInMbox (ch29), SPU_WrOutMbox (ch28), MFC_EAH/MFC_EAL (DMA address halves), and SPU_MFC_Cmd. MFC DMA is executed by do_dma_transfer(): GET copies main-memory EA -> LS, PUT copies LS -> EA. Atomics use GETLLAR (reserve a lock line) / PUTLLC (conditional store) backed by a global reservation table (g_reservations) shared with PPU lwarx/stwcx, so an SPU PUT can invalidate a PPU reservation. Interrupts modeled by spu_int_ctrl_t with class 0 (DMA align/errors) and class 2 (mailbox/tag-group completion), delivered to lv2_int_tag. A recompiler optimization: because MFC command + parameters are often compile-time constant, the transfer code is specialized and inlined for speed.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already maps VM memory as host_ptr=g_base+guest_addr with big-endian conversion at boundaries, which is exactly what makes do_dma_transfer cheap (a byteswap+memcpy between LS array and g_base). Transferable concretely: (1) model channels as small structs with the value+flags atomic encoding; (2) implement getllar/putllc against a single reservation table shared with the PPU path so cross-processor atomics work; (3) when an SPU function's MFC command operands are statically known, the AOT lifter can emit a direct memcpy/byteswap instead of a generic DMA call — a clean static optimization that mirrors RPCS3's runtime one.

dimensions.howItWorks: cellSpurs is implemented as HLE: it is reimplemented in C++ on the PPU side rather than running Sony's real SPURS SPU kernel. Core structs are CellSpurs (holds the SPU thread group spuTG, workload state arrays wklState1/wklState2, event queue/port infra, mutex/condvar primitives, handler threads), CellSpursTaskset (task grouping), and CellSpursJobChain (job queue). PPU 'handler' threads coordinate: they wait on workload readiness (handler_wait_ready), start/join SPU thread groups via LV2 syscalls (sys_spu_thread_group_start/join), connect event ports, and pump sys_event_queue_receive for exceptions/shutdown. SPURS is hard because it is deeply stateful, uses SPU mailboxes as semaphores, and depends on precise PPU<->SPU scheduling timing — so RPCS3 mixes HLE coordination with accurate low-level SPU execution of the actual workload code. Historically (2017-2018) getting SPURS right was the biggest single unlock; many games hung at boot waiting on a SPURS task that never completed.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp resolves HLE libs via 32-bit NID = SHA1(name)[:4], so cellSpurs entrypoints can be intercepted the same way RPCS3 intercepts the library call. Lesson: HLE the SPURS *coordination* (scheduler, taskset, jobchain bookkeeping) in C/C++ keyed on the NID, but still run the game's own SPU workload code (recompiled). Mirror the CellSpurs/CellSpursTaskset/CellSpursJobChain layouts byte-exactly because games poke those structs directly. Expect boot hangs to trace to SPURS tasks that never complete — a debugging signature to watch for. This is a known prerequisite for a large fraction of commercial titles to boot.

dimensions.dimension: PPU prior art: XenonRecomp / XenonAnalyse (closest match)
dimensions.howItWorks: XenonRecomp statically recompiles Xbox 360 PowerPC (with VMX128) to C++ — the closest analog to ps3recomp's PPU lifter and it hits the identical problems. Mechanisms: (1) Function detection via XenonAnalyse: function starts found from branch-link instructions, lengths from the .pdata exception directory (functions with stack frames have boundaries declared there); manual overrides in TOML. (2) Jump tables: detect the mtctr r0 / bctr pattern, dump tables to TOML, emit switch-case. (3) Indirect/virtual calls: a perfect-hash table where dereferencing a 64-bit pointer at (original_instr_addr*2) yields the recompiled function address; function addresses placed in memory after valid XEX regions, exported as macros in ppc_config.h. (4) PPC context struct passed to every recompiled function holds 32 GPR/FPR/VMX regs + CR/CTR/LR/XER/MSR, sized for setjmp/longjmp. (5) Big-endian: byteswap on every load/store; vector regs reverse the whole 16-byte value (so a dot product becomes WZY instead of XYZ). (6) Mid-asm hooks: inject a function at an instruction address without overwriting it (name/address/registers + return/jump conditionals). (7) Function patching via weak-linkage PPC_FUNC/PPC_FUNC_IMPL so hand-written replacements override recompiled bodies. Optimization flags (skip_lr, cr_as_local, xer_as_local, *_as_local) promote rarely-observed state to C locals. Built with Clang 18+ only. RSX-equivalent shaders are handled by the sibling XenosRecomp (Xenos microcode -> HLSL/SPIR-V), and UnleashedRecomp is the shipping Sonic Unleashed port.

dimensions.relevanceToPS3: This is the blueprint for ps3recomp's PPU side. Direct adoptions: use the PRX/SELF exception/unwind tables (PS3's .opd plus any .eh_frame-like data) the way XenonRecomp uses .pdata to recover function boundaries and lift recall above 72%; adopt the perfect-hash indirect-call table to resolve vtables/function pointers at runtime instead of failing statically; adopt mid-asm hooks and weak-linkage overrides so missing/buggy functions can be hand-patched without re-running the whole pipeline; adopt the per-register 'as_local' promotion to cut emitted-C bloat; and copy the whole-vector byteswap + index-swizzle convention for VMX/AltiVec (PS3 PPU VMX is essentially the same family as VMX128). XenosRecomp is the template for ps3recomp's RSX/NV47 shader path: decompile GPU microcode to a portable shading language rather than emulating the GPU.

dimensions.howItWorks: N64Recomp statically recompiles MIPS to C: addiu becomes ctx->r4 = ADD32(ctx->r4, 0x20); JAL -> direct call; JR -> switch-case for detected jump tables; branch delay slots handled by instruction duplication; jalr $25 -> LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r25)(rdram, ctx). It is driven by an ELF plus a TOML config (stubbed funcs, skips, instruction patches). Overlays (the N64 analog of dynamically-loaded SPU images) are handled two ways: statically-linked overlays use a runtime function lookup table for jalr; relocatable overlays emit RELOC_HI16/RELOC_LO16 macros so addresses are fixed up at load time against the section's current base. Single-file output mode lets you recompile just a patch and override functions via the linker. The same tool can recompile RSP microcode (the N64 vector co-processor) though RSP overlays aren't yet supported. Deps: rabbitizer (decode), ELFIO, toml11. The runtime (N64ModernRuntime) supplies the macros, overlay management, and dispatch; rendering is via the separate RT64 renderer.

co-processor (RSP) recompiled by the same engine
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: The overlay mechanism is the cleanest published model for ps3recomp's dynamically-loaded SPU problem: emit relocation macros (HI16/LO16 analog for SPU's absolute addressing) so a recompiled SPU image can be 'loaded' at different LS bases at runtime without recompiling — directly attacking the Red Dead absolute-addressing case. The LOOKUP_FUNC table is a simpler alternative to XenonRecomp's perfect hash for indirect SPU branches. The TOML 'skips/stubs/patches/jump-tables' config format is a proven schema ps3recomp could mirror for manual fixups. RSP-recompiled-by-the-same-engine validates ps3recomp using one toolkit for both PPU and SPU.

dimensions.howItWorks: 'Dusk' (released May 9 2026 by the TwilitRealm team, CC0; renamed 'Dusklight' on 2026-05-12) is a native PC/mobile port of The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess (GameCube). It is NOT a static recompiler and NOT an emulator: it is built on the zeldaret/tp *decompilation* project, where the entire game was hand-rewritten in C++ over ~5 years until all GameCube versions reached 100% byte-matching (Dec 2025). The recovered C++ source is compiled to native binaries; a cross-platform abstraction layer called Aurora (SDL-like) maps GameCube graphics/audio/controller calls to host platforms, with multiple selectable graphics backends. There is a separate, unrelated FPS game literally named DUSK, and an Xbox 360 recomp ecosystem (ReXGlue using Xenia's graphics backend; UnleashedRecomp) — but none of those is the 'Dusk' Twilight Princess port. So as a source of recompiler techniques, Dusk contributes essentially nothing; it is a decomp-reimplementation, the opposite end of the spectrum from ps3recomp's binary lifting.
techniques: decompilation to byte-matching C++ (not binary recompilation)
Aurora cross-platform abstraction layer (SDL-like) over GameCube APIs
selectable graphics backends
native compilation, no CPU simulation
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: Minimal/negative for the lifter: Dusk proves the *decomp* route (manual source reconstruction) is infeasible for the PS3 game library at scale, which is exactly why ps3recomp chose static recompilation. The one transferable idea is architectural: a clean SDL-like portability layer (Aurora) sitting between recompiled game code and host OS/graphics — analogous to ps3recomp's runtime (vm memory, LV2 syscalls, cellGcm->RSX backend). Treat the runtime as a stable HAL with swappable graphics backends (null/D3D12/Vulkan), exactly as Dusk swaps backends behind Aurora.

dimensions.howItWorks: RPCS3 does not run RSX shader microcode on a host shader core directly; it decompiles the RSX fragment/vertex microcode, reconstructs intent, and recompiles to SPIR-V via GLSLANG for the Vulkan backend (VKGSRender.h) or to GLSL for OpenGL. The command stream itself is a FIFO of NV47/Nvidia-family commands parsed by an RSX command processor. The XenonRecomp ecosystem takes the analogous approach for Xbox 360's Xenos GPU with XenosRecomp (microcode -> HLSL/SPIR-V) and ReXGlue reuses Xenia's graphics backend.
techniques: GPU microcode decompiled and recompiled to SPIR-V/GLSL (not interpreted)
FIFO command-buffer parser for NV47-family commands
backend abstraction (Vulkan via GLSLANG / OpenGL via GLSL)
sibling-tool pattern (XenosRecomp) for the GPU half of a recomp project
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp already plans cellGcmSys HLE -> RSX command processor (NV47 FIFO) -> null/D3D12/Vulkan, which matches RPCS3's structure. The transferable refinement: build a dedicated RSX-microcode-to-SPIR-V recompiler (the XenosRecomp/RPCS3 pattern) rather than trying to interpret shaders, and keep the FIFO parser separate from the shader translator. Reuse of an existing emulator's GPU backend (as ReXGlue reuses Xenia's) suggests ps3recomp could initially borrow RPCS3's RSX shader-decompiler logic to bootstrap.

dimensions.howItWorks: RPCS3 maps guest memory at vm::g_base_addr (0x0) with an unprotected mirror at vm::g_sudo_addr (+0x100000000); a global g_reservations table backs all atomics; syscalls route through g_ppu_syscall_table. The PPU enters recompiled code through ppu_gateway, an assembly stub using the GHC calling convention, and exits to the host every few blocks to run check_state() (handling cpu_flag::stop/exit/wait/pause/suspend) and unwind. Compiled code is cached on disk per-image. XenonRecomp/N64Recomp externalize all hand-tuning into TOML (function boundaries, jump tables, stubs, skips, patches, mid-asm hooks) and emit one C/C++ file per function (plus a single-file patch mode for overrides).
techniques: dual memory mapping: protected base + unprotected sudo mirror
global reservation table for cross-processor atomics
GHC-calling-convention gateway stub for host<->guest transitions
periodic check_state() with a cpu_flag bitset
TOML config as the manual-override surface
one-file-per-function output + single-file patch/override mode
on-disk compiled-code cache keyed per image
dimensions.relevanceToPS3: ps3recomp's host_ptr=g_base+guest_addr already matches RPCS3's mapping; adding a sudo/unprotected mirror is a cheap way to do fast internal writes that bypass guest page protection. A single shared reservation table is required for correct PPU/SPU atomics. The TOML-config surface (from XenonRecomp/N64Recomp) is the most directly copyable tooling idea: ps3recomp should accept a per-title TOML carrying function-boundary overrides, jump tables, NID stubs, instruction patches, and mid-asm hooks — turning the manual work of fixing the ~28% missed functions and indirect branches into reviewable config rather than code edits.

standoutInnovations: Content-keyed (hash-of-local-store) SPU compilation cache: compile lazily on first execution of an LS region and reuse by content, not by address — the only robust answer to dynamically DMA'd SPU images. The Red Dead Redemption case (same code loaded to different LS addresses due to absolute addressing) proves you must hash content and normalize relocations, not key on load address.

XenonRecomp's perfect-hash indirect-call table: dereference a pointer at (original_instr_addr * 2) to get the recompiled function address. A near-free O(1) runtime resolution for vtables/function pointers/switch targets that ps3recomp currently can't resolve statically — directly attacks the indirect-branch gap.

Using the exception/unwind directory (.pdata in XEX) to recover function boundaries and lengths. PS3 SELF/PRX carry analogous unwind metadata plus .opd; mining it should push ps3recomp's ~72% function recall substantially higher with no heuristics.

Mid-asm hooks + weak-linkage function overrides (PPC_FUNC/PPC_FUNC_IMPL): inject or replace behavior at any instruction address without re-running the whole recompile — a practical workflow for incrementally fixing games and HLE-ing hot functions.

SPURS as HLE-scheduler + LLE-workload split: reimplement the cellSpurs scheduler/taskset/jobchain in C++ on the PPU side (intercepted by NID) while still running the game's own recompiled SPU workload code. Mirror the CellSpurs structs byte-exactly because games poke them directly.

Whole-16-byte vector byteswap with index swizzle (dot product becomes WZY not XYZ): the correct, cheap way to reconcile big-endian VMX/AltiVec vectors with little-endian host SIMD — saves per-element swaps.

Relocatable-overlay macros (N64Recomp's RELOC_HI16/RELOC_LO16): emit relocation macros so one recompiled SPU image can be placed at multiple LS base addresses at runtime, the static-AOT analog of RPCS3's content-keyed JIT.

Recompiling GPU microcode to SPIR-V/GLSL (RPCS3 + XenosRecomp) instead of interpreting shaders, with the FIFO parser kept separate from the shader translator — the right shape for ps3recomp's NV47 RSX path.

Externalizing all manual fixups into a per-title TOML (function boundaries, jump tables, stubs, skips, instruction patches, hooks) so reverse-engineering effort becomes reviewable config rather than code edits.
verifiableClaims: RPCS3 implements cellSpurs as PPU-side C++ HLE (CellSpurs/CellSpursTaskset/CellSpursJobChain structs, handler threads, LV2 syscalls and event queues) rather than executing Sony's real SPURS SPU kernel image.

RPCS3's SPU recompiler compiles SPU code lazily at runtime keyed by the content of the function/block (not its load address) and caches compiled programs to disk (Spu-*-v3/v4.dat); Red Dead Redemption defeated naive caching because it loaded identical SPU code to different local-store addresses using absolute addressing.
sys_spu_image::deploy() in RPCS3 computes a SHA-1 hash over SPU image segments (segment types SYS_SPU_SEGMENT_TYPE_COPY/FILL/INFO) and applies patch_engine patches at load time.

XenonRecomp recovers function boundaries from the XEX .pdata exception directory, detects jump tables by the mtctr r0 / bctr pattern (dumped to TOML), and resolves indirect/virtual calls via a perfect-hash table indexed by the original instruction address multiplied by 2.

The 'Dusk' (renamed 'Dusklight') Twilight Princess PC port is a decompilation-based native reimplementation built on the zeldaret/tp project (which reached 100% byte-matching for GameCube versions by Dec 2025) using a cross-platform layer called Aurora — it is not a static recompiler or emulator.

RPCS3 models SPU channels with spu_channel (1-entry, atomic u64 value+flags) and spu_channel_4_t (4-entry inbound mailbox), and unifies PPU lwarx/stwcx with SPU getllar/putllc through a shared global reservation table (g_reservations).
